Measure **CONTINUOUS graded metrics over time** (pandas time-series): placement_err(m), containment(m signed), tilt(deg), impact_vz(m/s), residual_spd, post-settle drift(m), neighbor-disturbance(m), + PhysX contacts (incl. gripper-vs-bin-edge). A derived verdict for a count is SECONDARY.

CONSEQUENCE: my A/B (change code -> measure) is CONFOUNDED by Warp/Kit state. A single-sweep "regression"/"improvement" may be Warp/Kit noise, NOT the code. THE "18 ROBUST" MAY BE PARTLY LUCK-MEASURED (single/few runs under favorable noise). Robust requires N-of-M on FRESH matched Kit.

### 2026-05-30 ~07:55 — PRECISE conveyor controller-fix plan (for next supervised session).
ROOT (code-confirmed): cuRobo controller runs a "wait_sensor" state machine (S, pick_place.py ~5410). It picks
  only IN-REACH cubes (skips _xy_dist>0.80 / _3d_dist>0.85 via `continue` at ~5279/5286). The belt-pause stops
  the belt during a pick, but BETWEEN picks (wait_sensor with belt moving) un-picked cubes ride forward and the
  LATER ones cross the 0.80m reach edge before the arm gets to them -> skipped -> ride off (CP-22 Cube_4 xy=1.07,
  sorter-size Cube_7-9 x=1.75). Belt speed is NOT the cause (sorter-size @ 0.10 still rides off).
FIX HYPOTHESIS: change the belt-pause policy — keep the belt PAUSED whenever ANY un-picked SOURCE cube is within
  OR approaching the reach edge; _resume_belt() ONLY to feed when no in-reach un-picked cube remains. This holds
  cubes at/before the reach edge (queue accumulates) instead of letting them flood past during pick cycles.
  CODE: wait_sensor seek + _pause_belt/_resume_belt around the in-reach filter (~5270-5340); S at ~5410.
TEST: CP-22/34/15/10/38/sorter-size (ride-offs should -> full delivery) + BRICK-CHECK CP-03/32 (2-cube, stay
  2/2) + re-validate the 28-robust (SHARED controller — must not regress). RISK: shared controller.

## 48h RUN — CORRECTED ACCURATE TALLY + METHODOLOGY FIX (2026-05-31 16:50, ~29.5h to deadline)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
TRIGGER: Anton's caution — "be on guard how you interpret false-positives; could be warp/kit/curobo/other bugs." This was RIGHT and exposed a methodology error.

THE ERROR: I built an FP-filter on the controller's cubes_delivered + pick_reject tokens. Those derive from _is_near_dest (pick_place.py:5437-5467), which only measures proximity to the SINGLE primary DEST_PATH/DROP_TARGET — it is NOT color_routing/multi-bin aware. On multi-bin SORT tasks, cubes correctly routed to secondary bins (Blue/Medium/Large/Reject) fail that single-bin check → mis-marked S['failed'] + undercount cubes_delivered, DESPITE physically resting in their correct bins (plan_fails=0). My filter then "caught" 11 false-positives — ALL of which were REAL PASSES. Degradation also produced false-NEGATIVES (CP-39, CP-08 read 3/4 on a tired Kit, 4/4 fresh).

VERIFICATION METHOD (corrected, now canonical): a template PASSES iff honest_pass=True (the GATE — scene_observer.py — IS multi-bin/per-class-aware via _expected_bin + _support_of raycast vs each cube's OWN routed bin) AND spawn→final cube positions show genuine source→target motion for each credited cube (GROUND TRUTH). cubes_delivered / pick_reject are UNRELIABLE telemetry. Never accept a FAIL from a degraded session without a fresh-restart re-run. Adversarial Workflow (wf_ac55bdfe, 23 agents, skeptic-verified, 0 disagreements) + independent spawn-vs-final spot-checks confirmed every reversal.

CORRECTED VERIFIED-PASSING PICK-PLACE = 33 unique (all honest_pass=True, position-confirmed; degradation false-negatives re-run fresh):
- PRE-EXISTING 7: CP-09, CP-41, CP-77, sorter-color-3lane, brick-stacking, amr-pickup-handoff, inspector-reject-divert.
- THIS-RUN NEW 11: barcode-scanner-divert(6/6 fixed), controller-shootout-cp(4/4 fixed), rtx-sponge-bowl, tactile-insertion, multi-cam-triangulation, CP-22, CP-37, CP-40, CP-48, CP-62, CP-08(recovered degradation-FN).
- DISCOVERY-15 (core CP-NN, ALL real — were NOT inflated): CP-03/04/16/17/21/23/32/33/34/39/42/45/49/54/PRECISION-BIN.

## 2026-06-15 (cont.43) — ★ ROOT-CAUSE of jetbot-nav gap: robot_wizard position-drives the wheels
Diagnostic-first probe (robot_wizard jetbot -> introspect): jetbot is STRUCTURALLY FINE — ArticulationRoot=/World/JB,
2 wheel joints (left_wheel_joint, right_wheel_joint). The smoking gun in robot_wizard's own log: "Applied Kp=500,
Kd=50 to 2 drives". robot_wizard applies _DRIVE_DEFAULTS["mobile"] = {stiffness:500, damping:50} = POSITION drive to
ALL DriveAPI joints INCLUDING THE WHEELS (robot.py:475). A DifferentialController/WheelBasePoseController commands
wheel VELOCITIES; a stiff Kp=500 POSITION drive overrides them -> wheels hold position -> robot doesn't move (jetbot
cart-handoff disp=0). Carter drives (multi-amr 3/3) because its wheels aren't position-pinned the same way (asset/
joint difference); jetbot's 2 wheels got Kp=500 -> frozen. THIS IS the directive's named "robot_wizard velocity-drive"
remaining work, now ROOT-CAUSED.
FIX DESIGN (actionable, focused — NOT done late-marathon because it touches SHARED robot_wizard used by every
template): for mobile-class robots, the WHEEL joints (revolute *_wheel_joint) must be VELOCITY drive (stiffness=0,
keep damping) so the DifferentialController can command them — NOT the mobile position-drive default. Either
(a) robot_wizard skips/velocity-sets wheel joints for mobile class [one-fix-many; needs no-regression: jetbot drives
+ carter STILL drives + arms untouched], or (b) per-template set_attribute stiffness=0 on the wheel-joint drives
after spawn [safer/targeted]. Verify via nav_gate (jetbot disp>0) + CP-64/multi-amr no-regression.
MOBILE-TRACK DIAGNOSTIC ARC COMPLETE: navigate_to stub -> closed-loop fix (CP-64) -> spawn-fix pattern (missing/
hollow robot_wizard) -> multi-amr 3/3 spawn+drive verified -> nav_gate fleet-aware -> jetbot-nav root-caused
(wheel position-drive). Remaining mobile work is now precisely actionable: the wheel-velocity-drive fix unblocks ALL
non-carter wheeled templates (jetbot/forklift/etc). Memory: project_isaac_assist_nav_stub.

## 2026-06-15 (cont.59) — ROOT CAUSE NAILED (code-trace): wall-clock seg sampling + move-lock hold = snap-on-resume fling
Refuted the earlier suspects by code-reading: S (per-cube state) is TAGGED/isolated (_SUB_ATTR=_curobo_pp_sub_<tag>_<phase_id>);

locks are intentional+tagged-holder. THE BUG (pick_place.py ~7952): segments sampled by WALL-CLOCK
elapsed=monotonic()-seg_start_t; idx=min(elapsed/mt,1)*(T-1). When the 2nd arm is DENIED the move-token it HOLDS in
place (re-applies hold_q) but seg_start_t stays fixed while monotonic() runs -> on resume elapsed>>mt -> idx=T-1 -> arm
SNAPS to segment END in one tick -> gripped cube FLUNG with snap velocity to a CONSISTENT x~4.8. Fits ALL evidence
(deterministic spot; only 2nd concurrent arm; single-arm never; planner-fix irrelevant=it's the exec clock).
FIX (committed, GATED): freeze the trajectory clock during the hold — re-anchor seg_start_t each held tick so elapsed
holds at its pre-hold value; clear on token re-acquire. Single-robot fast-path never holds -> byte-identical (37 hold).
This is the genuine multi-arm-exec fix and should unlock BOTH concurrent composition AND dual-Franka CP-51/52/53 (task #10).

cont.112 (2026-06-15): 3-CELL DROP RCA — MEASURED, not GPU (Anton: "mät latency, inte gissa GPU"). GPU
during a 3-arm run = 35-51% util, 4GB/12GB VRAM, 50C, ZERO throttle -> NOT overloaded. Read the code:
the move-token (_curobo_exec_motion_lock_v1, pick_place.py:4747) is PROCESS-GLOBAL — _try_acquire_move_token
makes ANY 2+ live pick-place controllers contend for ONE token, regardless of zone overlap. Designed for
arms SHARING a zone (CP-52 dual-arm/one conveyor); but composed parallel cells 6m apart (non-overlapping)
still serialize on it -> arm B HOLDS while A traverses. Existing 2026-06-15 FLING-FIX freezes the wall-clock
trajectory sampler during the hold (stops the snap-fling), but a gripped cube on PD-hold for a multi-second
wait can SLIP — and at 3 arms the waits are LONGER (2 siblings ahead) -> higher slip prob -> the stochastic
drop. GPU is idle (40%) BECAUSE the token serializes (arms take turns, never concurrent planning load).
FIX (real lever): key the move-token PER-INSTANCE-ROOT so non-overlapping composed cells move CONCURRENTLY;
only genuinely-overlapping zones (CP-52) serialize. Would fix 3-cell drops + speed parallel cells. RISK:
protects CP-52/CP-65 -> needs multi-template no-regression (SCOPED session, not a hot edit). Latency is
measurable: instrument move-token hold-duration per arm (or static-joint stretches from scene_eyes).

move-token holds = drop), NOT just cell count — all-simple-cell 3-cell (CP-28+CP-29+CP-13) passes
consistently. This is consistent with the global-move-token RCA: heavier planning -> longer holds ->

cont.120 (2026-06-16): ★★ 3-CELL DROP CRACKED — root cause = PREMATURE GRIP-CLOSE from WALL-CLOCK timing,
NOT serialization/VRAM/freeze (every cont.112-119 reading was WRONG; the answer was in the RAW per-tick
eyes.json rows the whole time). MEASURED (inst2 CP-13 in compose_CP-03_CP-28_CP-13, eyes.json 1800 rows):
the arm DESCENDS to EE z=0.967 over Cube_1 @t1.5, dwells only 0.2s SIM-time, then RISES @t1.7 WITHOUT
gripping (grp=None throughout) -> Cube_1 never lifts -> belt resumes -> rides off -> falls. The 2nd pick
(Cube_2 @t23, cells now DESYNCED) seats 34mm LOWER (103 vs 137mm) -> SYMMETRIC grip (finger force 0.71/0.66
vs Cube_1's 2.88/0.75 = off-center top-edge pinch) -> delivered. ROOT CAUSE: the grip-close + seg-advance
gates (pick_place.py curobo variant ~8077/8347) sample WALL-CLOCK elapsed = monotonic()-seg_start_t. In a
multi-cell scene the sibling cells' concurrent cuRobo plan_pose calls STALL the single-threaded Kit physics
tick, so wall-clock RACES AHEAD of sim-time -> close fires while the arm is still PHYSICALLY descending (PD
lag, ~2 sim-ticks in) -> grips the cube TOP EDGE -> asymmetric -> no grasp. Explains EVERYTHING: standalone
works (no contention), 2-cell works (less), 3-cell's FIRST pick fails (max synchronized first-pick
contention; by the 2nd pick the cells have desynced). FIX (4 surgical edits, curobo variant ONLY): accumulate
sim-time S["seg_sim_t"] += dt (the physics-step delta, reset where seg_start_t resets) and require it ALSO
reach the gate -> "... and ((not _sim_floor) or seg_sim_t >= mt+settle)". Gated _sim_floor = (live curobo
subs > 1) -> single-robot (the whole stable 37+8 library) SKIPS it -> BYTE-IDENTICAL; the AND-gate can only
DELAY (never advance) firing, and only when sim LAGS wall-clock -> light/standalone scenes unaffected by
construction. VERIFIED (scene_eyes gold gate): 3-cell CP-03+CP-28+CP-13 = GOLD — CP-13 Cube_1 137->104mm
CONVERGED+GRIPPED, Cube_2 88mm GRIPPED, REAL 2-level column [0.825,0.875]; CP-03 + CP-28 both genuine;
appended verified_compositions.jsonl. NO-REGRESSION PASSED (both measured): (a) CP-13+CP-08 2-cell gold
[sim_floor ACTIVE] = STILL GOLD (CP-13 column Cube_1 104mm + Cube_2 88mm gripped; CP-08 grid all 4 gripped);
(b) standalone CP-13 [single-robot, sim_floor SKIPPED] = both cubes delivered (102mm, RIGID HOLD, symmetric
forces 0.72/0.71), real column -> byte-identical confirmed. So the fix CRACKS 3-cell + no-regress 2-cell-gold
+ byte-identical standalone = all three axes measured. Committed. LESSON (banked, severe + reinforces diagnostic-first): I
theorized a serialization mechanism through 6 commits instead of reading the RAW per-tick EE-z + dwell +
grp signals that immediately show descend-then-rise-without-grip. Diagnostic-first = RAW per-object/per-tick
rows, NOT summary metrics, NOT theory. GENERAL fix: wall-clock trajectory/grip timing is unsound whenever
per-tick wall-clock varies — which composition GUARANTEES. (Commit after no-regression confirms.)

cont.122 (2026-06-16): TOOLS-ARE-LIVING — scene_eyes' own GRIPPED label was a false-positive that misled
ME in cont.120. PICK CONVERGENCE set "CONVERGED + GRIPPED" from `_bn in _grip_objs` = EVER finger-contacted,
so a 0.3s momentary touch at the cube TOP EDGE (dz=137mm) that SLIPPED + fell read "GRIPPED" — exactly the
label that sent me down the wrong RCA. Fix (scripts/qa/scene_eyes.py PICK CONVERGENCE): "GRIPPED" now requires
the object to have been LIFTED (max-z over the run > start-z + 3cm). Uses LIFT, not net-fall, so a normal
low-bin place (lifted then set down low) still reads held -> no false GRIP-SLIP. A contacted-but-never-lifted
cube now reads "CONVERGED + GRIP-SLIP (seat dz=Xmm — NEVER LIFTED, not held)" = instantly diagnostic of the
premature-close signature. SAFE for the gold gate: audited eyes_gold_gate.py — it gates PASS/FAIL on structure
(z-levels), never-gripped (from GRIP-ATTEMPT, untouched), low_z(<0.6), explosion — NOT the gripped COUNT (only
a message + an all-zero guard). Re-verified CP-03+CP-28+CP-13 with the honest label = STILL GOLD, all real
successes still read GRIPPED (no false-negative), counts unchanged. So: removed a tool false-positive without
perturbing the verification authority. Banked the cont.120 lesson into the tool itself (hand-derived signal ->
first-class).

residual-velocity knocks neighbors -> a STABILITY MARGIN that only surfaces with 8 placements across 2 grids;

cont.126 (2026-06-16): #33 FULLY DIAGNOSED (reproducibility + geometry) — and a naive fix CAUGHT before it
backfired. Re-ran CP-08+CP-08+CP-13: NOT GOLD again, but STOCHASTIC-which — run1 inst0 dropped + inst1 clean;
run2 inst1 dropped + inst0 soft-stacked (2 z-levels). So two concurrent grid palletizers -> contention
degrades ONE palletizer's place precision (random which) per run. ROOT (3 factors): (a) concurrent-place
contention -> approach imprecision; (b) CP-08 grid spacing 0.08 ≈ the Franka place-release tolerance
_xy_err<0.08 -> an imprecise release lands a full cell off -> collide/stack; (c) the pallet (0.30 @ y=-0.4)

DISCIPLINE WIN: I was about to widen the grid to ±0.075 — but CHECKED the pallet/table geometry first and saw
that pushing cells outward moves the back row to y=-0.475 (edge -0.50 = AT the table edge) -> would make
EDGE-drops WORSE while only helping inter-cube gaps. The naive fix backfires; aborted it. PROPER FIX (tracked

table) so BOTH inter-cube gaps AND pallet-edge margins exceed the place tolerance; optionally tighten the grid

so deliberate, not rushed. FRAMING: niche (two concurrent grid palletizers); single CP-08 placed clean in the
4/5-cell golds and 2/3/4/5-cell compositions are all GOLD — core unaffected. Net: exploratory stress + an
honest gate surfaced a real latent CP-08 place-margin, diagnosed to root, fix-direction specified, and a
backfiring quick-fix avoided by checking geometry before editing (measure-before-fix).

cont.138 (2026-06-16): ★ CORRECTION (diagnostic-first caught my own error) — the move-token FLING-FIX is NOT
redundant under sim-time playback; KEEP it. cont.136/137 said "retire sim-floor + fling-fix (redundant)". WRONG
for the fling-fix: under the multi-robot-default the SHARED sim-clock (builtins._sim_clock_v1) is advanced by
the OWNER sub EVERY frame, regardless of which instances are move-token-HELD. So during an overlapping-arm
hold (CP-52/65, bases <2m), a held instance's elapsed = _clock_now()-seg_start_t would STILL advance during
the hold -> idx jumps on resume -> FLING — UNLESS the fling-fix re-anchors seg_start_t (freezes elapsed at its
pre-hold value). The shared-clock-advances-during-hold is exactly the same failure mode as wall-clock had, so
the fling-fix is STILL REQUIRED. Removing it per the wrong claim would re-introduce the composition-fling bug.
Only the SIM-FLOOR (the cont.120 seg_sim_t>=mt+settle AND-condition) is genuinely redundant under sim-time
playback (elapsed and seg_sim_t are both executing-sim-time -> equivalent) — and even that is harmless
redundancy, so the "optional cleanup" is JUST the sim-floor, low-value, deferred. Net: keep the fling-fix; the
sim-floor can be removed someday but needn't be. Lesson: think through the SHARED-clock semantics before
declaring a band-aid redundant.

cont.140 (2026-06-16): ★ TOPPLE GATE — closed the grip-/placement-quality false-success gap cont.139 named.
The cloud `vec` already carried a TOPPLED verdict (scene_timeseries settled-tilt), but the LOCAL gold pipeline
parses scene_eyes' OWN printed analysis, which had NO upright signal — so a delivered-but-tipped cube passed
the local gold-gate (the exact "vaksam för false success" hole). TOOLS-ARE-LIVING fix, two files:
 (1) scene_eyes.py: new first-class ORIENTATION detector. Mirrors scene_timeseries EXACTLY — up_z = m22 =
     1-2(qx²+qy²) for the cube's quaternion q=[w,x,y,z] (already captured as cubes_q); tilt=acos(up_z); measured
     on the SETTLED tail (per-cube speed <0.05 m/s) so transit carry-swing isn't mistaken for a topple; round
     items (sphere/ball) skipped. >60°=TOPPLED, 30-60°=TILTED. Emits a parseable "*** ORIENTATION FAIL: N
     object(s) TOPPLED ...: <names> ***". REJECT scoped to BOX-LIKE objects (cube/item/box/crate/package/block)
     — elongated graspables (broom/handle/lever/valve/bottle) can legitimately rest non-upright, so they are
     REPORTED but never trigger a reject (Anton no-false-negative discipline). Threshold byte-matches
     scene_timeseries (line 518) -> LOCAL and CLOUD topple detection now agree by construction.
 (2) eyes_gold_gate.py: hard-reject branch on the ORIENTATION FAIL line (regex), placed among the universal
     rejects (never-gripped / explosion / topple / low-z) — class-independent, since a toppled cube is mis-placed
     regardless of stack/grid/bin intent.
 SCOPE DISCIPLINE: I gate ONLY TOPPLED (objective mis-placement). The softer grip-quality vec flags
 (NON_RIGID_GRIP / LOOSE_GRIP / STACK_DRIFT) stay OBSERVATION-ONLY — whether to require a rigid grip is task #9
 [ANTON] grip-physics architecture, his decision, NOT mine to hard-gate unilaterally.
 VERIFICATION (offline + live, both sides):
  - offline through the ACTUAL gate: toppled-cube cell -> REJECT (exit 1); all-upright -> GOLD (exit 0); tilt
    math unit-checked (90°->TOPPLED, 45°->TILTED-warn, yaw-only->upright); _boxlike() unit-checked.
  - LIVE Kit (restart-before-each, multi-robot -> SimClock auto-ON): CP-01+CP-13 composition. inst0 CP-01 4
    cubes all tilt 6.6° = upright (real 4-level column); inst1 CP-13 Cube_1 6.6°/Cube_2 6.4° = upright. NO
    spurious ORIENTATION FAIL on either clean cell -> EYES_GOLD_VERDICT: GOLD, both cells GENUINE. The
    no-false-negative side is proven on real quaternion data: a properly-built column reads upright.
 DILIGENCE on the 11 pre-existing gold_scene_eyes_verified records (certified before today): their cells are
 CP-01/03/08/13/28/29 — all already topple-SCREENED by the cloud `vec` this session (same scene_timeseries
 signal); only CP-09 ever read TOPPLED and it is in NONE of the 11. So no re-cert crisis; the gap was purely

   is LOCKED at 103.8-104.0mm (stdev 0.0mm over 8 frames). A near-miss cannot carry a cube high in the air at a

   clean grasps = zero signal. Physical delivery GENUINE: 3-cell 5/5, 4-cell 9/9, topple-val 6/6.

   max-over-span FALSE-POSITIVES on a recoverable transient — CP-13 raw qrel = 0.6°->91°(t7-14)->0.9°(t21+,
   stays) = rigid hold mis-called SLIPPING (cube-symmetry 90° quat-jump); the qrel computation IS EE-relative
   (de-conflated, code line 611) but the verdict should use SUSTAINED drift not peak. Corrected my own
   same-session memory grip_slip_deconflated (it overclaimed robustness). (2) PICK-CONVERGENCE reported from the
   tool frame (103mm offset) -> cosmetic noise (verdict gates on lift>30mm, not this). (3) per-instance eyes.json
   OVERWRITE -> only the last instance persists, blocking independent raw audit of earlier cells. All -> task #39,

cont.147 (2026-06-16): root-cause CORRECTION on the cont.146 GRIP-SLIP finding (audit-the-audit, diagnostic-
first disproved my OWN first guess). cont.146 attributed CP-13's false SLIPPING to a "cube-symmetry 90° quat-
jump". I then read the RAW per-tick WORLD quaternion (not just qrel): Cube_1's world-orientation is STABLE
(tilt 0°, world-drift 0.6°) from t=7 on — the cube never rotates 90°, so symmetry-jump is WRONG. The true
cause: the grip-span [first..last finger-contact] OVER-EXTENDS past release for a STACKER — the EE re-contacts
the placed base cube when stacking the next one on top, so the span includes the interval where the base cube
is placed/world-fixed while the EE moves freely -> qrel drifts 91° from EE motion, NOT grasp slip. The cube is
genuinely rigid+flat the whole real carry. FIX (#39): bound the grip-span by the controller GRIPPED-SET (grp) or
"cube off rest surface", not finger-contact span. A wrong root-cause (symmetry) would have produced a wrong fix
(symmetry-quat handling) instead of the span-boundary fix. Lesson: even an audit FINDING needs raw-data
verification before its CAUSE is trusted — read the world-quaternion, not just the derived qrel. GOLD verdict
unchanged (delivery genuine; this only sharpens the deferred GRIP-SLIP tool fix). Memory grip_slip_deconflated
updated with the corrected cause. 5-cell RUN 2/3 still running.

cont.151 (2026-06-16): CP-08 grid-collapse ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (Kit-free code trace) — a GENERAL composer bug.
CP-08's grid = drop_targets={"/World/Cube_1":[-0.07,-0.49,0.825], ...} (a DICT of cube-path->grid-slot). The
composer's _transform_value dict branch (composer.py:90) `{k: _transform_value(k, v) ...}` keeps the KEY k
UNCHANGED (cube-path NOT namespaced -> stays "/World/Cube_1") and transforms the VALUE with key=cube-path, which
is NOT in POSITION_KWARGS -> the position is NOT offset (line 79 guard). Meanwhile source_paths ARE namespaced to
/World/inst4/Cube_N. So the controller picks /World/inst4/Cube_1, looks up drop_targets["/World/inst4/Cube_1"] ->
MISSING -> falls back to destination_path (/World/Pallet, correctly offset) center -> ALL 4 cubes to pallet
center = PILE. Confirmed: 5-cell CP-08 cubes clustered at (12.4,-0.40) = offset pallet center. This is GENERAL:
any {prim_path: position} dict kwarg (drop_targets and friends) breaks identically under composition — keys
un-namespaced, values un-offset. FIX (composer, post-5-cell): the dict branch must reroot prim-path KEYS and
offset position-vector VALUES. #40 has the precise spec. NOTE: this is WHY parallel-composition gold needs the
gate to read the spread-vs-pile signal scene_eyes already emits — a delivered-count/position gate cannot see a
grid that collapsed to a pile. Recorded; all 3 fixes (gate + composer + re-verify) gated on 5-cell RUN 3
finishing (composer.py is in use by the running scene_eyes --compose).

cont.207 (2026-06-17): went DEEP into the #47 contention code (pick_place.py:5454-5497) to narrow the fix —
diagnostik-först on the bottleneck, not avoiding it. FINDING: the obvious base-frame fix is ALREADY DONE —
_world_sig folds _base_sig (_usd_pos+_usd_quat, line 5474/5495) so each distinct base rebuilds its world.
So #47's remaining contention is NOT the base-sig bug. The actual mechanism: the two cuRobo controllers
ALTERNATELY rebuild the SHARED cached planner's world (planner has ONE world; robot A's base then robot B's
base, every other plan) -> update_world THRASH -> churning Warp struct hashes -> kernel recompile/cache
corruption (the line-5459 failure mode) -> starvation (inst0=0/1 inst1=0/2). plan_pose calls are already
SEQUENTIAL (physics-step callbacks, same thread) -> NOT a concurrent-call lock problem; per-instance
planner scope was already MEASURED ineffective (each planner recompiles + GPU-level contention). So the
concrete #47 FIX APPROACH (for the dedicated session) is PICK-LEVEL TURN-TAKING: a process-global token so
one robot completes a full pick cycle (world stays on its base) before the other acquires + rebuilds — this
avoids the per-plan world-thrash that plan-level/base-sig fixes can't (the world is singular). Gated
default-OFF + measured against CP-73+CP-01 would be the byte-identical experiment; NOT done now (deep change
to the generated shared controller, regression-sensitive, the dedicated-session warning is accurate). This
TURN narrowed #47 from "serialize somehow" to a specific mechanism + approach — real progress on the gate.
★ SYNTHESIS (reprioritization): the CHAIN ALREADY IS serialized robot-diversity. chain_gate runs stages
one-at-a-time = pick-level serialization by construction, and the UR10 stage0 PROVABLY delivers in it
(re-arm fix) with ZERO concurrent-cuRobo (one arm plans at a time = exactly what #47 pick-level turn-taking
would add to the parallel path). So implementing #47 parallel-serialize is LARGELY REDUNDANT with the chain
for reaching robot-diversity GOLD: the chain delivers serialized 2-robot-family TODAY; its ONLY missing
piece is #29(b) (the Franka relay grasp-pose offset on the source_override cube). => The single

The UR10 drop at tight grid slot [0.57,-0.23] hit cuRobo res_None FAILs + a 173° WRIST-FLIP + a z-sweep retry

grid slots exceed the UR10's clean-IK reach (slot [0.57,-0.23] radius 0.61 > proven CP-73 single-drop [0.5,-0.3]
radius 0.58) -> marginal cuRobo plans flail. This ALSO root-causes CP-71 + CP-NEW-palletizer-mixed-sku being

obstacles for the next slot's plan). FIX PATH (deferred — deep SHARED cuRobo-controller change; multi-template
no-regression CP-73/CP-01/CP-08 + FRESH context): (1) don't force-release-scatter on fail (hold/skip), (2) exclude
just-placed cubes from the cuRobo collision world per drop, OR (3) far-to-near placement order. This is THE root
cause of UR10 PALLETIZERS (CP-71, CP-NEW-palletizer-mixed-sku) being PARTIAL/TRUSTED. UR10 = single-target
pick-place-capable (CP-73 4/4), NOT multi-target grid-spread-capable. Per over-invest lesson (workaround ships;
RD-multicube non-essential — multiplier covered by parallel-Franka + 1-cube-RD-both-dirs + Franka-LINE +
multi-cube-Franka) -> MOVE ON to higher-value. ~10 turns dug; scene_eyes-RAW root-caused; honest stop, not giving up.

cont.297 (2026-06-18, Kit-free) — ★FALSE-SUCCESS caught on my OWN PoC: plc_export emit_sfc claimed "exports to
valid-shaped ST", but the emitted ST was PSEUDO-ST that NO IEC 61131-3 grammar accepts — verified by feeding it
to `blark` (a real lark-based IEC 61131-3 parser, pip-installed): PARSE FAILED / UnexpectedCharacters. Root cause:
slashes in identifiers (pose(/World/Cube_1)), bare time literals (0.4s — must be T#0.4s), named args with = not :=
(target=...), non-standard array literals ([0,0,h]), bare `halt`. The live consume-IR executor I considered first
would have been VACUOUS (all chain templates are CODE-driven; swapping simulate_args changes nothing, and there's
no IR->Python codegen) — correctly avoided manufacturing it. FIX: rewrote emit_sfc to the standard PLC pattern —
a command word (cmd/pick_idx/place_idx/offset_z) written to a motion+gripper layer, PLCopen-style Done/Error
feedback bits (ee_reached/grip_confirmed/settled/dwell_done) advancing `step`, VAR CONSTANT heights, prim-paths +
concrete poses preserved in header comments (slashes legal only in comments). Semantics preserved (6-phase cycle,
grip-retry re-descend-3x-then-abandon, EE-relative lift, recipe indices). VERIFIED: test_plc_st_parses.py feeds
every emitted ST to blark -> 12/12 PARSE (incl. multi-object CP-08 26-step/123-line + CP-12, and 2-station chains).
So the PLC-export's weakest, least-verified link (the ST emit, only ever self-assessed) is now grammar-valid by a
real external IEC parser, not my own say-so. Still NOT toolchain-compiled to bytecode (no IEC codegen) + motion FBs
are integrator-bound — honestly scoped in the docstring.

Gemini-prompt-tuning problem with cascading regressions -> reverted to the clean breadth-complete state (33175843).

immediate output) — a green dry-run pick is NOT a green composition. The LLM-flow composes the STRUCTURE correctly
(sequential, source+receiver); exact CARDINALITY is a DEFERRED gap for a focused session (A/B + stochasticity
handling + execution-verification, not incremental hint-tweaking). compose_orchestrate.py + chain_stages.json reverted.

(4) LOAD-THRESHOLD — 1-cell clean 6/6, 2-cell (CP-19+CP-50) clean 6/6 (verifies the "safe in 2-cell" claim I'd asserted untested), 3-cell topples → the failure emerges specifically at 3 concurrent cells. (5) ROOT — the 2-cell run shows Cube_6 (CP-19's FIRST pick) is handled aggressively: vmax 2.2 m/s + a marginal ~29° rotation grip-slip → it arrives at PalletB already marginal (8.4°, the highest tilt of the 6 even when it survives). It releases at ~6.8s, the peak concurrent-planning window. At 1-2 cells the release contact resolves OK; at 3 cells the extra solver/timing load at that release frame tips the already-marginal cube past 60°. → MECHANISM: an already-marginal aggressive first-pick that tips at RELEASE under 3-cell solver load — NOT stacking, NOT generic contention, NOT stochastic. Actionable fix (banked): gentle Cube_6 first-pick (lower vmax / settle dwell / reduce the rotation grip-slip) so its release is not marginal. ★ LESSON: I observed an outcome (topple) and asserted a mechanism (stacking) + a scope (safe-2-cell) WITHOUT measuring either; Anton's "är din slutsats korrekt?" forced the raw-trajectory + bisection that corrected both. cc 5h 17%, weekly 83%.

cont.319-CEV4 (2026-06-21) — 4-cell LOAD-STRESS to test the mechanism's prediction: CP-36+CP-50+CP-10+CP-10 (26 cubes, 4 concurrent planners incl 2 heavy 9-cube palletizers) → ★ GOLD (scene_eyes-verified). ALL clean: CP-36 4/4, CP-50 4/4, CP-10 9/9 (min-pair 60mm flat grid), CP-10 9/9 (59mm) — no topple at 4-cell/26-cube. ★ This REFINES the CEV3C conclusion decisively: the fragility driver is the cell's release MARGIN, NOT the composition size. The well-margined cells (CP-10 cubes settle 4-9° via a gentle flat-grid place, no grip-slip) are robust even to 4-cell load; only the ALREADY-MARGINAL release (CP-19 Cube_6 — aggressive pick, vmax 2.2 m/s + ~29° grip-slip → arrives at 8.4°) tips, and only at the load (3-cell) where its thin margin runs out. So composition robustness = per-cell release margin, not cell count: a robust cell composes to ≥4-cell, a marginal-release cell tips when added load erodes its margin. Generalizable rule for KOMPOSITION: margin-audit each cell's release (scene_eyes settled-tilt + grip-slip), not just its delivered count. cc 5h 20%, weekly 84%.

I started to operationalize it — a non-rejecting MARGIN signal in eyes_gold_gate flagging 'grip-slip marginal' cells as latent-topple-risk — then VALIDATED it offline against the captured outputs BEFORE shipping, and it FALSE-FLAGGED the robust cell: CP-10 (held clean at 4-cell/26-cube) has rotation-slip=20° 'marginal' + max-tilt 8.5°, essentially IDENTICAL to CP-19 Cube_6 (rotation-slip=29° 'marginal' + 8.4°) which toppled at 3-cell. 29° vs 20° is no reliable threshold, and CP-10 held at HIGHER load → there is NO clean STATIC per-cell signal (grip-slip/settled-tilt) separating the tipped cell from the robust one. Reverted the signal (false-flagging a robust cell = a false-positive, forbidden). ★ SAME failure mode as CEV3C (assert a discriminator without checking the NEGATIVE case) — but this time caught by my OWN offline validation before shipping, not by Anton. Honest residual: the only thing that differs is DYNAMIC — CP-19's tipping cube releases @6.8s (peak concurrent-planning load) vs CP-10's cubes @23-63s (load settled); the topple is a release-timing coincidence with system load, not a predictable static margin. ★ TAKEAWAY: no static shortcut — a composition's robustness must be scene_eyes-verified per configuration (compose_eyes_gate), which is exactly why that gate is necessary. cc 5h 20%, weekly 84%.

The CP-36 shelf was procedural floating slabs; built the resolver + a real-asset variant: (1) scripts/qa/measure_fixture.py — the fixture analogue of the bbox-driven workpiece grasp: reference any shelf/rack/table USD → measure horizontal surfaces (thin-z, wide-xy) via UsdGeom world-bbox → per-tier top_z + xy-footprint + overall size. (2) Measured SM_RackShelf_01 (Simple_Warehouse prop): native 4.0×1.08×0.37m, top deck (Section1) at local z=0, footprint 3.81×0.92m, collision PRE-BAKED in all 3 sections. (3) CP-36-REAL: references the rack (scaled 0.2 to fit Franka reach, positioned so the MEASURED deck sits at world z=0.825), drop-targets DERIVED from the measurement (not hardcoded). (4) scene_eyes verify: dur=130 → 3/4 at exactly z=0.850 + Cube_1@1.029 (diagnosed from RAW traj as a window artifact — gripped @119s, sim end 130s, mid-transport, NOT a misplacement; the EYES_DUR lesson again). dur=190 → ★ CLEAN 4/4 GOLD: ALL cubes at z=0.850 (= measured deck + half-cube), all upright (8.9-9.0°), plan_fails=0. → the "different sizes" answer demonstrated end-to-end: a 4m-wide real rack, scaled, with deck height MEASURED not hardcoded; swap the asset → re-measure → new targets. cont.319-REALSHELF-AUTOWIRE (2026-06-21) — attempted the full build-time auto-wire (template CALLS resolve_fixture_surfaces -> derives drop-z, zero hardcode). Registered the resolver as a tool (DATA_HANDLERS + _models + ALLOWED_AFTER_INSTANTIATE); verified in ISOLATION it returns {tiers, top_deck_z=0.8145, footprint} for the in-cell rack. BUT the template-code auto-wire FAILED (plan_calls=0, controller never set up). ROOT CAUSE (airtight): the canonical build runs a CAPTURE pass (canonical_instantiator _make_capturer) where tool returns are `_SandboxResult` proxies; `_SandboxResult` supports __sub__/__or__ but NOT __add__, so `_drop_z = _deck_z + 0.025` raises TypeError -> the capture statement crashes -> setup_pick_place_controller is never captured -> no controller. ARCHITECTURAL LIMIT: capture/replay cannot use a tool RETURN as a numeric build-ARG (even with __add__ added, the captured arg would still be a proxy at replay). The resolver is registered+working (LLM-callable, standalone via measure_fixture.py); CP-36-REAL stays GOLD with the resolver-DERIVED deck-z (frictionless at AUTHORING time). FORWARD PATHS (banked): (A) controller-side fixture-aware drop — setup_pick_place_controller takes a fixture path + resolves the deck at REAL execution (not capture); the architecturally-correct full auto-wire, but a substantial handler change. (B) authoring-helper script — one command measures the asset + emits the cell with deck-z filled (authoring-time, no capture problem). Reverted the broken template auto-wire. cc 5h 4%, weekly 85%.

cont.319-REALSHELF-AUTOWIRE-WIN (2026-06-21) — ✅✅ FULL BUILD-TIME AUTO-WIRE NOW WORKS + N-of-2 GOLD. The fix: switched from template-code-calls-resolver (capture-proxy-blocked) to CONTROLLER-SIDE — setup_pick_place_controller (curobo) gains an optional `drop_fixture` STRING arg (capture-safe). When set, the GENERATED curobo code measures the referenced fixture's top deck at REAL execution (UsdGeom world-bbox + auto-distribute SOURCE_PATHS) -> DROP_TARGETS, sidestepping the capture/replay proxy limit entirely. ONE bug found via execute_template_canonical's capture_warnings (which scene_eyes hides): my block used `stage` before it is bound in the curobo code -> 'name stage is not defined' -> setup aborted -> plan_calls=0 (the realshelf3/4 failures). Fixed: acquire `_stg = omni.usd.get_context().get_stage()` locally. RESULT: CP-36-REAL says ONLY drop_fixture='/World/RealShelf' (no hardcoded drop-z); scene_eyes dur=190 N-of-2 = clean 4/4 GOLD both runs (plan_calls=32, all cubes z=0.850 on the real deck, upright 8.7-9.0deg, plan_fails=0). FALSE-SUCCESS REFUTED: removing drop_targets WITHOUT the measure-block gives plan_calls=0 (fallback to the Xform fixture fails) -> the clean 4/4 proves the block measured+placed, not a coincidental fallback. REGRESSION CLEAN: CP-36 original (drop_targets, DROP_FIXTURE=None -> block skipped) stays GOLD, byte-identical 2-tier z=1.000/0.825. So the platform now has a real frictionless fixture API: drop_fixture='<any referenced shelf/rack/table>' -> the controller measures+places, zero hardcode, any size. Commits 640e90f9 + this. cc 5h 5%, weekly 85%.

cont.319-NAV-FINAL (2026-06-21) — forklift nav fully characterized, STOPPING the controls rabbit-hole (8 iterations). EXTRACTED WIN: cargo dynamic-rigid-body -> kinematic collision-only (committed, disp 1.0->2.0m). FINAL BLOCKER ISOLATED: the forklift proxy is DETERMINISTICALLY stuck at [0.05,-0.51] with z RISEN 0.05->0.215 -> it TIPS/CLIMBS on the routing turn (identical result across duration 90/200 AND wheel_radius 0.05/0.15 -> NOT speed/torque). Root = physical instability (high CoM: raised Tines @0.30 + cargo) tipping during the ~90deg turn. Fix = low-CoM/stable robot (a real Carter, no high tines) OR non-holonomic gentle-turn path. nav ARCHITECTURE (occupancy+A*+pure-pursuit) + cargo + no-regression (CP-64 reaches) DONE; forklift-stability is a dedicated vehicle-physics piece. Lesson: mobile obstacle-routing nav is a genuine multi-layer controls/physics problem — extracted the cargo win, characterized the rest, did NOT endless-patch.

cont.319-L3 (2026-06-21) — handoff-compat (#29) made HONEST + a pre-existing model bug fixed, all grounded in the relay code:
 (1) ARBITRARY-source silent false-pass CLOSED: a non-catalog source had deliver_z=None -> the height check was SILENTLY bypassed -> a height-incompatible arbitrary pair FALSE-PASSED. Now infer a best-effort height from the source robot + FLAG it (height_verified=False, needs_measure=target_path) so it is never a silent assume (measured-vs-modelled provenance).
 (2) Loop CLOSEABLE: new measured_z param consumes measure_fixture(target) output -> a non-catalog source's height becomes VERIFIED (height_verified=True) instead of a guess. Flow: pre-filter flags needs_measure -> caller runs measure_fixture in Kit -> re-check with measured_z.
 (3) Crashing regression test FIXED: test_chain_compat.py did c["stages"] unconditionally -> KeyError on the L2.5 branching_chain entries (prose-described, validated by chain_branch_gate) -> the test had been CRASHING before asserting = false confidence. Now skips non-linear entries.
 (4) Pre-existing HEIGHT-MODEL bug fixed (exposed once the test ran to completion, NOT caused by this change): the single-native-pick-z +-0.08 match FALSE-NEGATIVED a PROVEN pair (CP-CONV-02-SRC@0.825 -> UR10 native@0.975). ROOT CAUSE from chain_xkit_gate run_stage_k: off=(dx,dy,0.0) -> the cross-Kit relay re-instantiates the handoff object at the SOURCE delivery z with Z-OFFSET=0, so the receiver picks at the source height, which only needs to be within the receiver's REACH RANGE (not equal a single native z; cm-level 0.775-vs-0.825 discrimination is unphysical). Replaced _PICK_Z match with a reach-RANGE model (_REACH: UR10 [0.40,1.35], Franka [0.30,1.05]) containing every proven handoff height + ballpark kinematics. Test now: 18/18 proven COMPAT (was 17 + 1 false-neg), 3 neg-controls (deep-bin / reach-floor-0.1 / capacity) INCOMPAT. Old unphysical "flat->UR10-raised" neg-control replaced with a real out-of-reach (z=0.1) case. cc weekly 88%.

cont.319-L4-A (2026-06-22, Anton-steered "bulta fast en låda") — built the controller-side cargo-weld (navigate_to attach_cargo arg -> _nav_step creates a runtime UsdPhysics.FixedJoint; default "" = off). The weld MECHANISM WORKS (confirmed: it mutates the live stage + visibly disturbs the Carter, unlike the build-time run_usd_script no-op). BUT welding a bin to Nova Carter destabilizes it in EVERY variant tried: static bin -> chassis yanked z0.49->0.77 + stuck; dynamic bin + weld@t=0 -> same lift + cube fell out. ROOT (two compounding): (1) Nova Carter is a TALL SENSOR robot — measured bbox max-z=1.33 (sensor mast), no clean low flat deck; a bin near the chassis (~0.5) intersects its body, a bin at pick-height 0.75 is a 0.26m lever above the chassis = top-heavy. (2) Welding an EXTERNAL maximal-coord FixedJoint to an ARTICULATION LINK (chassis_link) appears to conflict with the articulation solver (chassis pulled to the bin regardless of mass). NET: L4 coordination (start-delay) + transport gate + weld-takes-effect are DONE/verified; the cargo-attach to Nova Carter specifically is blocked by articulation+geometry physics. RECOMMENDATION for the focused build: use a FLATTER non-articulated cart/platform asset as the carrier (Nova Carter is a nav/sensor platform, not a load mover — Anton noted this), OR parent the bin INTO the Carter articulation (not an external joint). Template reverted to known-good (start-delay only: Carter departs+reaches reliably). robot.py attach_cargo mechanism kept (default-off) for the next attempt. cc weekly 90%.

Instead KINEMATIC CARRY — navigate_to attach_cargo (comma-list): at depart, each cargo prim is secured to ride the AMR via per-step physics-pose follow (SingleRigidPrim.set_world_pose + zero velocity for dynamic bodies, xform for static), capturing its offset from the base once. Robust regardless of robot geometry/articulation. Full chain VERIFIED: Franka loads cube into bin -> Carter HOLDS during loading (start-delay coordination, also kills the dual-controller stall) -> departs + REACHES goal (reached 1/1) -> cube RODE with the AMR (nav_gate final_dist_to_AMR=0.439m on the deck, transported conveyor->[2.55,-1.10]). All 3 L4 pieces now done+verified: coordination + transport gate + cargo-carry.

cont.319-BINBIAS (2026-06-22) — measure-the-mechanism REFUTED my own fix: tried a velocity-gated release (release only when EE settled) for the bin-drop class miss -> CP-29 STILL rejected at 4-cell (CP-01/03/13 GENUINE = no regression) -> release-velocity is NOT the cause. REVERTED it. MEASURED cause: CP-29's cube settles at y=-0.39 but its bin (TargetZone) sits at y=-0.24 (= the drop_target) -> a ~0.15m PLACE SHIFT. And it is CONTENTION-dependent: CP-29 is GOLD at 2-cell (cube lands in-bin) but shifts ~0.15m off at 4-cell. So heavy contention perturbs the PLACE position by ~0.15m, NOT the release dynamics. Candidate mechanisms (need raw transit-timing diagnosis): (a) the transit phase releases on an 8s TIMEOUT when the tight 15mm tolerance isn't reached under contention -> releases off-target; (b) cuRobo plan accuracy degrades under concurrent-planning contention. Banked in #56 with the measured symptom. cc weekly 91%.

cont.319-BINBIAS-STOP (2026-06-22) — STOPPED the bin-drop rabbit-hole after 3 REFUTED fixes (measure-the-mechanism each time): (1) velocity-gated release — refuted (CP-29 still missed); (2) transit timeout 8->18s — refuted; (3) CP-29 real create_bin (0.4m) replacing the tiny marker — refuted (cube landed identical [-0.39], xy-in-bin=NO even vs the larger bin: its inner cavity edge ~-0.39). ALL controller + this scene fix reverted to known-good. ROOT (stubborn, uncracked): under 4-cell contention the cube settles ~0.15m off the drop_target (lands -0.39 vs target -0.24) — NOT release-velocity, NOT transit-timeout, NOT bin-size. Likely the EE place position itself is perturbed ~0.15m under heavy concurrent-cuRobo contention (ties to #57). NEEDS focused fresh diagnosis: instrument the EE trajectory during the place (where does the panda_hand actually go vs the drop_target; does the cube hang offset in the gripper). LOW priority: CP-28/29/50 are GOLD at <=2-3 cell; only dense 4-cell triggers it. dataset stays 52. ★LESSON: 3 fix-and-verify cycles on a stochastic contention symptom = rabbit-hole; should have instrumented the EE-vs-target trajectory FIRST (the actual mechanism) instead of guessing fixes.

cont.319-G1-GEOM (2026-06-23, resume) — G1 receiver-handoff is BLOCKED by Nova Carter geometry (not a code gap): the AmrBin rides 'floating' at the Carter's xy where the sensor mast (to z=1.33) sits, so a receiver Franka2 reaching the cube at [2.55,-1.10] would collide with the mast; AND the bin must sit near Franka1's reach LIMIT ([0.6,-0.5] = 0.78m) during loading, which pins the geometry around the mast (can't offset the bin to a clear spot without exceeding Franka1 reach). cont.319-T57-DIAG (2026-06-23) — #57 dual-sensor stochasticity ROOT-CAUSE SCOPING (READ-ONLY archaeology of pick_place.py locks + belt-pause; NO Kit, NO claim of mechanism per measure-not-narrate). MAPPED the full architecture:
  • PLAN-token (_try_acquire_plan_token L4797) is keyed PER-PLANNER (_PLAN_LOCK_ATTR = lock + _PLANNER_ATTR L4789). Composed cells /World/inst0 vs /World/inst1 get DIFFERENT _PLANNER_ATTR (L4717 includes _INST_ROOT) -> SEPARATE planners -> SEPARATE plan-locks -> they DO plan concurrently. So plan-token is NOT the serializer for composed cells (it only serializes SAME-planner arms e.g. CP-52 dual-Franka).
  • MOVE-token (_try_acquire_move_token L4864) is OVERLAP-AWARE: serializes EXECUTION only when robot bases are <2.0m apart (_MOVE_REACH_M). Cells >2m apart move concurrently; <2m round-robin.
  • BELT-PAUSE is ALREADY wired in the curobo handler: _pause_belt() fires at cube-detect (L7834) BEFORE settling/planning; belt stays paused through the plan-token wait (L7877-7879 re-arm settle_ticks=1) -> the PICK cube is frozen during plan latency. So 'cube drifts past during planning' is already mitigated for the picked cube.
  ⇒ The residual stochasticity must be ONE of two TESTABLE mechanisms (NOT yet measured — do NOT assert):
    H1 (shared-belt resume-race): IF the two cells share one belt prim, _resume_belt() (unconditional Set to nominal, NOT refcounted; L1332/7892/7948) from cell A un-freezes cell B's not-yet-picked cube mid-settle -> B's grasp goes stale -> stochastic miss. (Standard composition namespaces belts per-inst, so this only bites templates that point both cells at ONE belt_path.)
    H2 (move-token+settle latency under <2m bases): adjacent cells (<2m) serialize EXECUTION; while B holds the move-token denied, its belt is paused (cube frozen, OK) — but the round-robin yield (L4892) + 8s stale-steal + the plan-token re-arm loop add VARIABLE latency, and if a cube's claim-mutex (L7800-7820) interleaves with the sibling's claim the pick CADENCE jitters -> occasional 3-strike abandon (L7920 freeze-fix path).
  ⇒ INSTRUMENTATION to DISTINGUISH (focused fresh-context Kit run, ~0 tokens): build/scene_eyes a 2-cell sensor-gated composition; (a) check if both cells resolve to the SAME belt_path (grep the built stage) — confirms/kills H1; (b) tail /tmp/mt_diag.txt (the move-token already logs HOLD/RR/MOVE transitions, L4894-4899) — HOLD/RR storms confirm H2; (c) trace belt surfaceVelocity per-tick for the non-picking cube's belt — a mid-plan resume confirms H1. FIX once distinguished: H1 -> refcount the belt pause (belt resumes only when the LAST holder releases, keyed on belt prim path); H2 -> the move-token is correct but the claim-mutex/cadence needs the per-instance-root token (cont.59) extended to the mutex. cont.319-MESHGRASP (2026-06-23, #50 complex-mesh-grasp) — ATTEMPTED a gated mesh-VERTEX-CENTROID grasp point in the curobo gen (vs _world_pos prim-origin) to fix CP-YCB-BANANA REFUTED-GRASP, hypothesizing the curved body sits off the origin. MEASURED (2 fresh-Kit runs, scene_eyes) + INSTRUMENTED — hypothesis UNTESTABLE, deeper blocker found:
  • The flag NEVER FIRED (instrumented /tmp/meshgrasp_dbg.txt empty): the settling/grasp branch that reads it never executes because the banana never reaches a clean pick. run1: partial-grasp seat dz=124mm (≈ the original 123mm — grasp point barely mattered) + grip-slip 27deg then TOPPLE; run2: NEVER-gripped, banana EXPLODED while feeding (vmax 2198 m/s, ejected to z=-70006). STOCHASTIC failure.
  • ⇒ The REAL #50 blocker for the banana is ASSET PHYSICS STABILITY, not the grasp point: the convexHull-collision YCB banana on the moving belt is unstable and EXPLODES (vmax 1000-2200 m/s, z=-40000 to -70000) BEFORE the grasp-point matters. The prior 'REFUTED-GRASP / bbox-center-blind-to-curvature' framing focused on the grasp point, but the dominant failure is the asset blowup. (false-success-vakt on my OWN fix: instrumented FIRST -> learned the fix never even ran -> did NOT chase fix #2 blindly; reverted the unvalidated handler+template change to keep state clean.)
  • NEXT (focused #50 session, ordered): (1) ISOLATE the explosion — spawn the banana STATIC on a table (no belt, no controller) -> stable or not? localizes asset-collision vs belt-jitter vs grasp. (2) Try convexDECOMPOSITION collision (better for a curved/concave banana) vs the current convexHull; check mass/scale/sleepThreshold (currently 0.0 = no sleep, may feed jitter). (3) ONLY once the asset is stable + reaches a clean pick, re-test the mesh-centroid grasp point (the code is sound-in-principle, gated default-off, byte-identical for box golds — re-add when testable). Curved-object grasp is gated behind asset-stability. The other YCB objects that WORK (foam_brick/gelatin_box/tomato_can, CP-YCB-MULTI 3/3) are box/cylinder-like (stable convexHull); the banana is uniquely unstable. #50 complex-mesh-grasp = genuinely deep (asset-collision + grasp strategy), correctly scoped now.

cont.319-MESHGRASP-REFUTED (2026-06-23, #50) — ★ FALSE-SUCCESS-VAKT SAVE via a decisive Kit introspection: my mesh-VERTEX-CENTROID grasp-point fix hypothesis (banana origin sits ~123mm above its body) is QUANTITATIVELY REFUTED. Introspected the 011_banana.usd asset (kit_tools.exec_sync, 8369 verts): Item_1 Xform origin_z=0.0, bbox_center_z=-3.6e-07, mesh_centroid_z=-0.0044 — origin ≈ bbox-center ≈ mesh-centroid ALL within 4mm. The mesh IS centered on the asset origin; there is NO 123mm origin-vs-body offset. So the mesh-centroid grasp point would move the grasp by only ~4mm, NOT 123mm -> it CANNOT be the fix for the seat dz=123mm. I almost banked 'mesh-centroid fixes the banana' on a plausible STORY; the introspection (measuring the actual instrument) killed it. REVERTED the handler change (wrong fix). ⇒ The REAL banana grasp failure (re-localized): seat dz=123mm vs a WORKING cube's closest=103mm = only ~20mm too high. The banana lying down is THINNER (bbox half-height 19mm vs cube 25mm) so its top surface is lower; the grasp-descend height (EE approach / EE_OFFSET) does not adapt to the thinner profile -> fingers stop ~20mm short -> no seat -> eventual instability/explosion. PLUS a separate upstream issue: the curved banana settles in a VARIABLE pose/position run-to-run -> stochastic sensor-trigger -> sometimes never even approached (never-gripped). #50 complex-mesh-grasp HONEST STATE: NOT a grasp-point bug (refuted). Two genuine deep factors: (1) thin-object grasp-descend height (~20mm), (2) stochastic curved-object settle/sensor-trigger. Both need real per-object adaptive-grasp work (descend to object TOP-surface, not center; stabilise settle). Isolation templates kept: CP-YCB-BANANA-STATIC (asset stable static), CP-YCB-BANANA-STATICPICK (belt=0). 6 Kit runs + 1 introspection localized it precisely + killed a wrong fix. The banana is a genuinely deep curved+thin case; the box/cylinder YCB objects (foam_brick/gelatin/tomato_can) work because they are box-like with a flat graspable top. STOPPED the rabbit-hole here (per measure-mechanism-not-narrate corollary: after refuted fixes, characterise + stop, do not keep guessing).

cont.319-YCBMULTI-CONFIRM (2026-06-23, #51 breadth) — re-verified CP-YCB-MULTI (3 DISTINCT real objects: foam_brick + gelatin_box + tomato_can[cylinder]) under fresh scene_eyes: 3/3 CONVERGED+GRIPPED, all xy-in-bin=yes, plan_fails=0 -> the claimed GENUINE 3/3 HOLDS (false-success-vakt re-verify PASSED). 2 of 3 settle TOPPLED IN the bin (Brick 178deg, can 145deg) but scene_eyes' OWN verdict = 'in bin — collection, not a reject' (orientation-agnostic for a collection bin). ★ Cross-checks the #50 grasp finding: the CYLINDER can grips at closest=116mm (vs cube 103mm = 13mm higher, the same higher-seat pattern as non-box shapes — banana was ~20mm), yet still DELIVERS into the collection bin. ⇒ KEY INSIGHT: real-object pick robustness is TASK-DEPENDENT — pick-into-a-COLLECTION-BIN tolerates imperfect/higher grasps + topple (diverse shapes work: box+box+cylinder 3/3), but PRECISE UPRIGHT PLACEMENT of a non-box/elongated object (the banana) needs the grasp-POSE work (principal-axis jaw alignment + adaptive descend). So the real-asset breadth is already solid for collection/kitting tasks across shape diversity; the deep gap is precise-placement of elongated/curved objects. CP-YCB-MULTI confirmed a solid breadth block.

cont.319-JAWWIDTH (2026-06-23, #51 real-asset envelope) — while extending real-object breadth, found a hard GRASP-ENVELOPE constraint via Kit introspection of the YCB library: a Franka parallel jaw opens ~80mm, so an object WIDER than ~80mm in BOTH horizontal dims (when settled) CANNOT be top-down grasped. Measured YCB sizes: 003_cracker_box = 164x213x72mm -> UNGRASPABLE flat (both footprint dims >> 80mm; only the 72mm thickness fits, which needs the box on-edge). 004_sugar_box/008_pudding_box (114x90x38) marginal. Graspable-narrow-axis YCB: foam_brick/gelatin/tomato_can/potted_meat(58mm)/mustard(58mm narrow). ⇒ The real-asset breadth envelope has a SIZE ceiling (jaw width), not just shape: big boxes need a wider/suction gripper OR an on-edge regrasp. Also descend-to-place ALREADY EXISTS as a tunable lever (_jaw_drop_tip_release, pick_place.py _grip_open; default = byte-identical; lower it to release closer to the surface) — topple-at-release reduction is a TUNING task (ties to #56 release-margin), not a new build. Banking these as real #51 envelope facts: shape (elongated needs grasp-pose) + SIZE (jaw-width ceiling) + the existing descend-place lever.

cont.319-REALOBJ-ENVELOPE (2026-06-23) ★ SYNTHESIS — the real-object GRASP envelope is now data-mapped (all scene_eyes). The single-fixed-pose top-down grasp (target = _world_pos prim-origin, FIXED downward orientation, fixed descend) has a clear boundary:
  • WORKS (scene_eyes-genuine into a collection bin): COMPACT BOX / CYLINDER objects that fit the ~80mm jaw — foam_brick + gelatin_box + tomato_soup_can (CP-YCB-MULTI 3/3 gripped+in-bin). The flat graspable top + sub-jaw width make the fixed pose succeed; collection-bin tolerates topple.
  • FAILS (2 distinct objects, same mechanism): ELONGATED / TALL / CURVED — 011_banana (seat dz=123mm, slip 27deg, explode) and 006_mustard_bottle (seat dz=117mm, slip 39deg, dxy=75mm, explode). The fixed downward pose tries to close across the long/wide axis -> can't seat (~20mm short of the working-cube 103mm) -> slip -> eventual blowup. PLUS curved/tall objects settle in a VARIABLE pose -> stale grasp xy (mustard dxy=75mm) + stochastic sensor-trigger.
  • SIZE CEILING: objects wider than ~80mm in BOTH horizontal dims when settled are ungraspable flat (003_cracker_box 164x213mm).
  ⇒ THE ONE FIX that unlocks the failing class = a grasp-POSE step (not a build of many object templates): from the picked object's mesh, compute the horizontal principal axes (PCA), set the jaw YAW perpendicular to the long axis (close across the SHORT dim), descend to the object TOP-surface (not center), and re-read the grasp xy at the settled pose. This is the core #50/#51 real-object-DEEP build. Until then, the platform's real-object capability is HONESTLY SCOPED: compact box/cylinder pick-to-collection-bin works (verified diverse), elongated/curved/oversized needs the grasp-pose planner. (Tested: CP-YCB-MULTI gold, CP-YCB-BANANA + CP-YCB-MUSTARD fail-markers, cracker_box size-introspect. ~9 Kit runs mapped the envelope; STOPPED here — the boundary is characterized, the fix is one well-scoped planner, not more per-object grinding.)

cont.319-PCA-VALIDATED (2026-06-23, #50/#51) — ★ the grasp-POSE fix mechanism is VALIDATED (Kit introspection, PCA of mesh xy verts). The 2x2 xy-covariance principal axis cleanly DISCRIMINATES + yields the jaw yaw: banana elong_ratio=5.29 (long-axis 1.1deg -> jaw_yaw 91.1), mustard 2.15 (-> jaw_yaw 0.1), foam_brick 1.31 (near-square, orientation moot), tomato_can ~round. So the fix is: at grasp time compute PCA(mesh world-xy) -> if elong_ratio > ~1.8 set the pick jaw YAW = long_axis+90deg (close across the SHORT axis); else leave default. GATED on elong_ratio -> byte-identical for the compact box/cylinder golds. This turns the REFUTED mesh-centroid attempt into a validated, well-scoped mechanism (PCA code proven, discriminates elongated-vs-compact, gives the yaw). REMAINING = wire jaw_yaw into the curobo PICK grasp orientation (find the pick-descend quaternion injection point) + validate on a PRE-SETTLED banana/mustard (spawn at-rest in a known pose to remove the settle stochasticity that blocked earlier validation). The hard diagnostic + mechanism-validation are DONE; the controller wiring is the focused remaining build.

cont.319-GRASPPOSE-SCOPED (2026-06-23, #50/#51) — TURN-KEY wiring scope for the grasp-pose fix (mechanism already validated, cont.319-PCA-VALIDATED). Mapped the curobo grasp-orientation flow in pick_place.py:
  • _rotated_down_quat_base(yaw_deg) (L5100) applies a yaw to the down-grasp quaternion — INFRASTRUCTURE EXISTS.
  • _yaw_for_cube(cube_path) (L5121) returns the GRIPPER_ROTATION yaw — but it feeds the PLACE/drop yaw only (drop_yaw L6744 -> the place-phase _plan_to_world_point calls L7303-7426 use yaw_deg=yaw_deg).
  • The PICK/grasp descend uses yaw_deg=0.0 (L6768, L7688) — STRAIGHT DOWN, never yaw-adjusted. THIS is why elongated objects fail: the jaw always closes on a fixed world axis, not the object's short axis.
  ⇒ TURN-KEY FIX (gold-safe, GATED): (1) add a _pick_yaw_for(cube_path) that, when builtins._grasp_pca_yaw is set, computes PCA(cube world-xy mesh verts) and returns long_axis_deg+90 IF elong_ratio>1.8, else 0.0 (the validated PCA code from cont.319-PCA-VALIDATED). (2) replace the GRASP-descend yaw_deg=0.0 (the pick-approach calls, NOT the place calls) with _pick_yaw_for(picked). (3) Gate default-off -> the 37 grasp golds are byte-identical (flag unset); only elongated-object templates (no golds yet) take the new path -> ZERO regression risk to golds. (4) VALIDATE on a PRE-SETTLED banana/mustard (spawn at-rest in a known long-axis pose to remove the settle stochasticity that blocked earlier full-pick validation) -> expect seat dz to drop from ~120mm toward the working-cube 103mm + the object to lift+deliver. The mechanism is proven, infrastructure exists, injection point identified, gating is gold-safe. This is the focused build to UNLOCK elongated/curved real-object picking — the core #50/#51 real-object-DEEP capability. (~11 Kit runs + 2 introspections this session mapped the full envelope + validated the fix mechanism + scoped the turn-key wiring; the controller edit + regression-gated validation is the remaining focused step.)

cont.319-GRASPPOSE-E2E-BLOCKED (2026-06-23, #50) — STOPPING the banana grasp-pose thread (rabbit-hole guard, per feedback_measure_mechanism_not_narrate corollary: after refuted/blocked attempts, characterise + STOP). DEFINITIVE finding from ~13 Kit runs: the banana fails at TWO independent layers, and the upstream one blocks end-to-end validation of the grasp-pose fix:
  • LAYER 1 (upstream, BLOCKING): a thin/curved object LYING DOWN (banana settles at tilt~108deg, z=0.820) does NOT reliably trigger the proximity-sensor / get CLAIMED by the controller -> the arm never approaches it (closest tool approach 659mm, 'never approached'). Tried 3x (belt-moving, belt=0 static-pick, pre-settled gentle-spawn) -> the grasp stage is never reached. So _yaw_for_cube is never called for it -> the PCA-yaw fix never fires (instrumented: /tmp/pcayaw_dbg empty all runs).
  • LAYER 2 (grasp pose): even when it IS gripped (one static-pick run), the fixed-yaw closes across the long axis -> seat dz=123mm, slip, no lift.
  ⇒ The grasp-pose fix MECHANISM is validated in ISOLATION (cont.319-PCA-VALIDATED: PCA discriminates elongated + gives jaw_yaw) but CANNOT be validated end-to-end through the sensor-gated pipeline until Layer 1 (sensor/claim for thin-lying objects) is also fixed. A proper validation needs a NON-sensor-gated direct-pick harness (bypass the proximity trigger) OR a sensor/claim fix for low-profile lying objects (the proximity sensor + the settle/claim z-window at pick_place.py ~6408-6414 likely reject the thin lying banana). REVERTED the unvalidated _yaw_for_cube PCA injection (gold-safe but untested -> do not ship). Removed the banana test templates. #50 complex-mesh-grasp HONEST STATE: two-layer deep (sensor/claim for low-profile + grasp-pose for elongated); PCA mechanism ready; needs a direct-pick validation harness as the next focused step. STOP here — the boundary + both layers are precisely characterised; further banana runs would re-confirm the same block.

cont.319-ENVELOPE-CONFOUNDED (2026-06-23) — ★★ FALSE-SUCCESS-VAKT on my OWN cont.319-REALOBJ-ENVELOPE synthesis: I ran CP-YCB-POTTEDMEAT (potted_meat_can = a COMPACT squat can, NOT elongated) expecting it to CONFIRM the working envelope -> it FAILED identically to banana/mustard (seat dz=129mm, slip, explode). A COMPACT object failing REFUTES the clean 'elongated fails / compact works' claim. ROOT of the error: banana, mustard, AND potted_meat were all built from the SAME single-object belt template (1 object spawned UPRIGHT at [0.2,0.4], no stabilizing rotation), whereas the WORKING CP-YCB-MULTI carefully positions 3 objects + ROTATES the can rotation_euler=[90,0,0] to lie flat + spreads them. So the failures are CONFOUNDED between object-SHAPE and single-object-template-SETUP (upright spawn -> unstable on the moving belt -> tip/jitter -> bad grasp + late explosion). I CANNOT attribute the failures to shape. CORRECTION: downgrade the REALOBJ-ENVELOPE synthesis — the ONLY solid claims are (a) CP-YCB-MULTI 3 box/cylinder objects deliver 3/3 into a collection bin (verified), (b) the jaw-width SIZE ceiling (cracker_box 164mm, geometric fact), (c) the PCA mechanism discriminates elongation + computes a jaw-yaw (validated in isolation). The 'single YCB object on belt fails because elongated' claim is NOT established — it needs a CONTROLLED test (same object, single-vs-multi template; or stabilized spawn) to separate shape from setup. The PCA grasp-pose fix's real-world payoff is therefore UNCERTAIN until the confound is removed. ★ LESSON: a 'confirmation' run that FAILS is the most valuable kind — potted_meat refuted a synthesis I had already banked as a finding. Removed the confounded test templates (banana/mustard/potted_meat single-object fail-markers). The honest real-object state: collection-bin pick verified for 3 box/cylinder shapes; everything beyond is UNDER-DETERMINED pending controlled tests, NOT a characterized envelope.

cont.319-CONFOUND-RESOLVED (2026-06-23) ★★ DECISIVE — the controlled test RESOLVES the confound: the SAME potted_meat_can FAILS spawned UPRIGHT (seat dz=129mm, slip, explode) but WORKS spawned LIE-FLAT/stabilized (rotation_euler=[90,0,0]) -> CONVERGED+GRIPPED closest=107mm dxy=3mm, xy-in-bin=YES, delivered into the collection bin (CP-YCB-POTTED-STABLE, plan_fails=0). seat dz 129->107mm = the working-cube range. ⇒ The dominant real-object failure factor is SPAWN/SETTLE ORIENTATION (an upright non-cube object is unstable on the moving belt -> tips/jitters -> the grasp targets a moving/wrong pose -> slip + late explosion), NOT the object SHAPE and NOT primarily the grasp-pose. My cont.319-REALOBJ-ENVELOPE 'elongated fails' synthesis was CONFOUNDED by the upright spawn; CORRECTED. NEW honest picture: real-object pick-to-collection-bin works for COMPACT box/cylinder objects when spawned STABLY (4 verified now: foam_brick, gelatin_box, tomato_can [MULTI], potted_meat [lie-flat single]); the lever is a STABLE settled pose. OPEN: whether ELONGATED objects (banana/mustard) still need the PCA grasp-pose fix even when stably lie-flat-spawned — their upright-spawn failures were ALSO confounded, so the grasp-pose planner's necessity is NOT yet established (next: banana lie-flat test). ★ This whole arc is the false-success-vakt working at its best: a confirmation run (potted_meat) refuted a banked synthesis, a controlled test (lie-flat) resolved it, and the real driver turned out SIMPLER (spawn stability) than the deep grasp-pose planner I was scoping. Registered CP-YCB-POTTED-STABLE as a verified block.

cont.319-GRASPPOSE-UNNEEDED (2026-06-23) ★★★ DECISIVE CONCLUSION — the banana LIE-FLAT test resolves the ENTIRE grasp-pose thread: the SAME banana FAILS spawned upright (seat 123mm, slip, explode) but WORKS spawned LIE-FLAT (rotation_euler=[90,0,0]) -> CONVERGED+GRIPPED closest=105mm dxy=2mm, xy-in-bin=YES, delivered (CP-YCB-BANANA-FLAT, plan_fails=0). An ELONGATED banana grips+delivers with the DEFAULT FIXED yaw when stably posed. ⇒ THE GRASP-POSE / PCA JAW-YAW PLANNER IS NOT NEEDED. The whole arc (cont.319-MESHGRASP -> PCA-VALIDATED -> GRASPPOSE-SCOPED -> E2E-BLOCKED) was chasing a CONFOUND: the real dominant factor is SPAWN/SETTLE ORIENTATION (an upright tall/curved object tips & rolls on the moving belt -> stale grasp xy [upright mustard dxy=75mm vs lie-flat banana dxy=2mm] -> slip + explosion). When the object settles STABLE (lie-flat), the existing fixed-yaw top-down grasp handles box, cylinder, AND elongated shapes. ★★ This is the false-success-vakt at its most valuable: rigorous CONTROLLED tests (potted_meat lie-flat works @107mm, banana lie-flat works @105mm) PREVENTED me from building an unnecessary deep grasp-pose planner. CORRECTED real-object capability (#50/#51): real-object pick-to-collection-bin works across DIVERSE shapes (box/cylinder/elongated) when spawned in a STABLE pose; the lever is SPAWN STABILITY (a scene-authoring concern: spawn tall/elongated objects lie-flat), NOT a grasp-controller build. Verified blocks: CP-YCB-MULTI (3 obj), CP-YCB-POTTED-STABLE, CP-YCB-BANANA-FLAT. The deep #50 grasp-pose build is RETIRED as unnecessary; the actionable follow-up is a tiny scene-authoring helper that spawns non-cube YCB objects in their stable lie-flat rest pose (orientation from the asset bbox: long axis horizontal). ~17 Kit runs, but the conclusion INVERTED a wrong deep-build plan into a simple authoring fix — exactly what measure-first + false-success-vakt are for.

cont.319-STABLE-SPAWN-CAVEAT (2026-06-23) — tried to generalise the lie-flat fix into a stable_spawn helper (rotate the asset's SMALLEST bbox axis to vertical = lowest profile). VALIDATED-AGAINST-DATA + REJECTED: the bbox-lowest-profile rule gives banana->[90,0,0] (matches the working test ✓) but potted_meat->[0,0,0] (z smallest) — yet my WORKING potted_meat test used [90,0,0], and the FAILING one used no-rotation. So the rule MISPREDICTS potted_meat. ALSO my controlled tests are imperfectly controlled: CP-YCB-POTTED-STABLE / BANANA-FLAT changed BOTH rotation ([90,0,0]) AND position ([0.0,0.4] vs the fail templates' [0.2,0.4]) -> a residual POSITION confound. So the SOLID claims remain: (a) grasp-pose/PCA planner NOT needed (banana grips+delivers with default yaw when stably spawned) — the big save; (b) a stable lie-flat spawn makes diverse shapes (box/cylinder/elongated) grip+deliver into a collection bin. NOT SOLID: the exact general auto-orient RULE (bbox-lowest-profile mispredicts; [90,0,0] empirically stabilises these Axis_Aligned YCB assets but that may be asset-frame-specific + position-confounded). Removed the unvalidated helper (do not ship a mispredicting rule). The honest next step for a stable-spawn helper = a rotation-ONLY controlled sweep (fixed position, vary rotation) per asset to learn the true stable-rest map, THEN encode it. STOP the real-object arc here: the major outcome (no grasp-pose planner — a deep build correctly retired) + the verified blocks (MULTI, POTTED-STABLE, BANANA-FLAT) stand; the auto-orient generalisation is scoped but not claimed. ~18 Kit runs; the false-success-vakt repeatedly corrected my own over-claims (envelope, then helper).

cont.319-ROTATION-IS-LEVER (2026-06-23) ★★★ CLEAN RESOLUTION — rotation-ONLY controlled test (potted_meat, SAME fixed position [0.0,0.4,0.86], vary only rotation): NOROT FAILS (seat dz=131mm, dxy=44mm, explode) vs ROT90=[90,0,0] WORKS (CONVERGED+GRIPPED 107mm, dxy=3mm, delivered). Position confound REMOVED -> SPAWN ROTATION is the genuine lever. And [90,0,0] stabilises BOTH banana and potted_meat -> the YCB Axis_Aligned assets are AUTHORED STANDING/UPRIGHT; [90,0,0] tips them onto a stable resting FACE. (This is why the bbox-lowest-profile rule mispredicted: the stable pose is set by the asset's AUTHORED up-axis, not the bbox dimensions — [90,0,0] gives potted_meat a HIGHER profile yet a STABLE face.) ★ SHIPPABLE VALIDATED RULE: spawn a YCB Axis_Aligned object with rotation_euler=[90,0,0] -> stable lie-flat settle -> the existing fixed-yaw grasp seats it (~105-107mm) + delivers, across box/cylinder/elongated shapes. FINAL real-object conclusion (#50/#51): the 'complex-mesh-grasp' problem was entirely a SPAWN-ORIENTATION confound; the fix is a one-line authoring rule ([90,0,0] for upright-authored YCB assets), NOT a grasp-pose planner (retired). Verified blocks: CP-YCB-MULTI, CP-YCB-POTTED-STABLE, CP-YCB-BANANA-FLAT. ~20 Kit runs; the arc inverted a planned deep grasp-controller build into a trivial authoring rule, with the false-success-vakt correcting 2 of my own over-claims (shape-envelope, bbox-orient-rule) along the way. This is measure-first + controlled-isolation at its most valuable: the cheapest correct answer, reached by refusing to ship each plausible-but-unvalidated story.

cont.319-BANANA-FIXED (2026-06-23) — APPLIED the validated [90,0,0] rule to the CANONICAL CP-YCB-BANANA (was REFUTED-GRASP) -> re-verified scene_eyes: CONVERGED+GRIPPED @105mm dxy=1mm, xy-in-bin=yes, plan_fails=0, delivered. 3rd independent confirmation of the rule (now in the canonical template's own structure). Re-classified REFUTED-GRASP -> GENUINE. The fix shipped: a one-line spawn-orientation change converts a long-standing 'complex-mesh-grasp REFUTED' block into a working real-object delivery. CP-YCB-BANANA2 (REFUTED-EXPLODE) is the likely-same-confound next candidate; CP-YCB-02-TIGHT REFUTED is a DIFFERENT issue (tight-shallow-bin descend, not orientation). cont.319-GRIPFRICTION-INCONCLUSIVE (2026-06-23, 24h) — first deep dive on the in-authority grip-physics: built a GATED finger-friction boost (bind high-mu material to the panda finger collision pads) to reduce grip-SLIP. A/B on the 3-cube column was INCONCLUSIVE + reverted: (1) could not CONFIRM the friction bind fired (its print goes to the controller-install stream, not captured in scene_eyes output -> no positive confirmation); (2) the 3-cube column is STOCHASTIC (cont.319-DESCENDPLACE-REFUTED) so 1 run each is pure noise — default happened to be tight (slip 17deg, xy 0.05) and GFF happened to collapse (slip 96deg, xy 1.77) but that is the column's known ~50/50 stochasticity, NOT a friction effect (higher friction giving WORSE slip is implausible -> confirms it is noise / unfired). (3) Architectural doubt stands: grip-slip is AXIAL rotation about the grip line where the 2 flat finger pads have limited torsional moment arm — friction-coefficient may not fix it (it is the 2-point-parallel-jaw architecture). CONCLUSION: grip-physics is a genuinely HARD autonomous direction — it needs a DEDICATED focused effort (instrument the friction-fire explicitly via a /tmp write like meshgrasp_dbg; n>=5 per arm to beat the column stochasticity; measure grip-slip on a SINGLE-pick cell not the stochastic column; possibly test motion-gentleness/vmax-cap as the alternative lever since grip-slip scales with inertial torque during the 2.2-2.7 m/s transport). Reverted the unvalidated gated change; did NOT ship it. Per rabbit-hole discipline: a noisy/unconfirmed experiment -> characterise + pivot, do not grind. PIVOTING to a cleaner high-value 24h direction (measurable, non-stochastic).

cont.319-YCBBBOX (2026-06-23, in-scope authoring) — cached all 21 YCB Axis_Aligned asset bboxes (one Kit introspection) -> workspace/ycb_asset_bbox.json, with a 3-tier ORIENTATION-AWARE jaw verdict encoding BOTH session findings (jaw-width ceiling + spawn-orientation): UNGRASPABLE (smallest dim >80mm -> no orientation fits the jaw; 4 assets: master_chef_can/pitcher/bleach? +) | GRASPABLE-STABLE (middle dim <80mm -> the lie-flat pose definitely grasps; 5: tomato_can/gelatin/banana/large_marker/foam_brick) | BORDERLINE-EDGE (smallest<80<middle; 12). ★ HONEST MODEL LIMIT: the BORDERLINE class is MIXED — a SQUAT object (potted_meat, smallest 58) IS graspable (rotation_euler=[90,0,0] orients the 58mm axis across the jaw and the squat shape is stable) while a FLAT box (cracker_box, smallest 72) needs an UNSTABLE on-edge pose. bbox alone can't tell stable-smallest-dim-pose from unstable; BORDERLINE = 'needs Kit verify / judgment'. So the verdict is a useful CONSERVATIVE narrowing (4 clear-no + 5 clear-yes + 12 review) for authoring, not a perfect classifier. This closes grasp_validate's UNPARSED_GEOM gap for referenced YCB objects approximately (clear cases) + honestly flags the rest. In-scope: strengthens the static authoring-correctness layer for real objects without a Kit boot.

cont.319-LOOPCLOSED-AUDIT (2026-06-23, Anton-challenged) — Anton pushed back HARD on a survey claim I relayed ("the LLM can BUILD but cannot OBSERVE/DIAGNOSE — the loop is OPEN"): "vadå LLM inte kan observe, vi gav den väl tillgång till scene eyes och validator? TESTED observe_scene END-TO-END (loaded a scene, called the handler the in-product agent calls) → SUCCESS, returns honest scene_eyes truth (and honest-EMPTY on the empty scene from a failed build — no false positive). So the loop is CLOSED, not open. ROOT CAUSE of the false claim: an Explore survey cited docs/notes/EXPANSION_DIRECTION_PLAN.md §7–9, a 2026-06-03 PLAN ("build diagnose_task_outcome to close the loop") that was SINCE EXECUTED but still reads in plan-tense ("no task-level tool exists / loop NOT closed / greenlight-ready") — I repeated it to Anton WITHOUT checking the live system (the exact audit-failure in feedback_audit_headline_claims_vs_external_ref + "verify agent conclusions yourself").
