cont.319-YMERGE-MECHANISM-CORRECTION (2026-06-23) — corrected my OWN earlier hypothesis before it became a stale claim (the exact failure I just cleaned for Anton in EXPANSION doc). The banked "Cube_L2 reach = spawn-geometry fix" is WRONG: read the role_defaults/code_template geometry — all 6 cubes funnel to the SAME pick sensor [0.4,0.40] (two lanes y=0.20 + y=0.60 merge to y=0.40 via belt surface_velocity), and are picked THERE. So spawn position is irrelevant to reachability; the other 5 cubes pick fine at the same point. REAL mechanism (measured, not narrated): scene_eyes OBJECT-OBJECT CONTACTS showed heavy cube-cube collisions at the merge (Cube_L2|Cube_L1, Cube_R1|Cube_L1, Cube_R2|Cube_R1...) -> Cube_L2 is DISPLACED off the pick point by a merge collision and the arm can't close the last ~18mm (121mm vs 103mm for clean picks). This is the inherent Y-MERGE SINGULATION-TIMING problem (cubes must arrive one-at-a-time; two lanes colliding at the merge is the hard part) — NOT a geometry nudge. A real fix = singulation control (stagger lane spawn/cadence, or sensor-gated single-claim with merge-pause) = a deep controller/timing effort, correctly NOT pursued now (rabbit-hole on a single non-trusted cell). Refutation stands; cell stays honestly REFUTED. Discipline: measure-the-mechanism caught my own narrated-hypothesis.

cont.319-SIZEWEIGHT-RESOLVED (2026-06-23, Anton: "stochastic = cop-out, vi vill ha UPPLÖSNING") — Anton corrected my methodology: don't terminate at "stochastic"; RESOLVE the deterministic mechanism (that's what scene_eyes is FOR). Applied to the size-weight sorter trusted exemplar (Franka:size-weight-sort = CP-NEW-sorter-size-weight, "9/9 DELIVERED 2026-06-14" count-only). scene_eyes N-of-2 (dur=360, Kit-restart between) = DETERMINISTIC (NOT stochastic): IDENTICAL failing cubes both runs (Cube_2 toppled-outside; Cube_3/4/5/6 tilted 37-47deg; Cube_1/7/8/9 clean). RESOLVED from raw eyes.json positions: size/weight sort routes 6 light->LightBin but only 3 heavy->HeavyBin; setup_pick_place_controller drops all same-class cubes at ONE point (bin centre). 3 cubes = stable short tower (HeavyBin all upright dxy~0.00); 6 cubes OVERFILL one drop point + cascade -- dxy grows 0.01->0.06->0.09->0.11->0.23 and z rises, so 4 tilt + the 6th (Cube_2) lands 0.23m out = OUTSIDE bin -> topples. So "9/9 DELIVERED" is orientation-blind: only 4/9 cleanly upright; ORIENTATION FAIL fires -> would fail the gold-gate. ORIENTATION-REFUTED in verified_status (surgical edit, original preserved). MECHANISM RESOLVED (deterministic bin-overfill at a single drop point), not labelled stochastic. FIX (banked, in-scope): raster per-class drops across the bin floor via DROP_TARGETS (palletizer grid mechanism) instead of one point -- needs color_routing to compose with positional drop_targets (handler change). ★METHOD LESSON (Anton): a per-run-varying failure is NOT "stochastic" -- the variation has a deterministic cause; measure it to resolution. Vein tally: y-merge REFUTED (merge-collision singulation) | size-weight ORIENTATION-REFUTED (bin-overfill) | inspect-reject + barcode + CP-13 HOLD. 2 trusted/catalog golds were orientation-blind count-claims; both now resolved deterministically.

cont.319-OVERFILL-MECHANISM-CONFIRMED (2026-06-23) — closed the count-only-sorter vein with a PREDICTIVE test (the resolution Anton demanded, made falsifiable). The size-weight resolution (LightBin overfill: 6 cubes at ONE drop point cascade, 3 stack clean) PREDICTS that CP-NEW-sorter-color-3lane (balanced 3 red + 3 green + 3 blue = 3 per bin) should be CLEAN. Fresh scene_eyes (dur=300): CONFIRMED — all 9 CONVERGED+GRIPPED, ZERO topple, ZERO tilt, three textbook 3-high towers (z=0.790/0.850/0.910 per bin). So the mechanism GENERALIZES + is proven by successful prediction: orientation failure in these sorters is DETERMINISTIC bin-overfill — cubes dropped at one bin-centre point form a stable tower at <=3 but cascade at >=6 (threshold ~4-5). NOT stochastic. Dual outcome: (a) CP-NEW-sorter-color-3lane gold GENUINELY HOLDS (9/9 upright, balanced); (b) the size-weight refutation mechanism is confirmed. The banked fix (raster DROP_TARGETS across the bin floor instead of one point) matters precisely when any single bin receives >~4 cubes. ★ This is the methodological win from Anton's "stochastic=cop-out" correction: a per-run-varying topple was resolved to a deterministic, PREDICTIVE mechanism. Vein FINAL tally: y-merge REFUTED (merge-collision singulation, deterministic) | size-weight ORIENTATION-REFUTED (bin-overfill, deterministic, N-of-2 identical) | color-3lane + barcode + inspect-reject + CP-13 HOLD (verified clean). 2 real catches, mechanisms fully resolved, 1 systemic fix identified + banked.

cont.319-RASTERDROP-FIX-SCOPED (2026-06-23, banked with design) — scoped the systemic fix for the bin-overfill mechanism (raster per-class drops instead of one bin-centre point). The drop position is computed by THREE _bin_drop_pos variants in pick_place.py (native @2653, spline @3384, curobo @4999 — size-weight uses curobo); each consults COLOR_ROUTING (class->bin) and returns the bin CENTRE +0.05 for EVERY routed cube. FIX DESIGN: (1) track a per-bin placement counter (builtins-scoped, per robot+phase like the existing subs); (2) when a bin's count exceeds a guard threshold (~3-4, size-aware: floor(bin_footprint / cube_footprint) per layer), offset the drop x/y into a raster grid across the bin floor (reuse the palletizer DROP_TARGETS grid math) instead of the centre; (3) GUARD: <=threshold cubes keep the current centre-drop -> ZERO regression for single-cube + small-bin cells (CP-01/CP-13/color-3lane balanced-3 all stay byte-identical). VERIFY PLAN: size-weight should go 4/9->9/9 upright (the 6 LightBin cubes raster into a single layer instead of a 6-tall cascade); regression sweep = CP-01 (single), CP-13 (stack/column — must still stack ON purpose, so the raster guard must EXCLUDE intentional stackers via a stack flag), color-3lane (balanced 3/bin), barcode, CP-08 grid. RISK: broad (3 code-paths + every bin/sort cell) -> deserves a FOCUSED session with the full regression sweep, NOT a rushed tail-end edit. Banked here with complete design; mechanism fully resolved (cont.319-OVERFILL-MECHANISM-CONFIRMED). ★ NOTE the stack/column subtlety: CP-13 INTENTIONALLY stacks (3-tower is the GOAL there) -> the raster fix must distinguish 'overfill cascade' (bad, sort bins) from 'intended column' (good, stackers) via the template's stack/column intent, else it would break the stack golds.

cont.319-RASTERDROP-REVERTED (2026-06-23, no-regression discipline) — the cont.319-RASTERDROP fix worked for size-weight (4/9->9/9 upright N-of-2) but the regression sweep CAUGHT a deterministic side-effect, so I REVERTED it (git safety net, no shipped regression). MECHANISM (A/B-resolved, deterministic NOT stochastic): the offline scan found exactly TWO >4/bin color-routed cells -- size-weight (fixed) and CP-BRANCH-SRC-SW (LightBin:6, same pattern). A/B on CP-BRANCH-SRC-SW: PRE-FIX = 9/9 gripped + 5 in-bin topples (its own overfill cascade); WITH-FIX (N-of-2 identical) = 8/9 -- Cube_3 THRASH-NO-CONVERGE @121.8s, 200mm dxy, never gripped, ends OUTSIDE. cont.319-RASTERDROP-MECHANISM-REFINED (2026-06-23, DIAGNOSTIK-FÖRST, 3 hypotheses refuted) — resolved the CP-BRANCH-SRC-SW raster regression deeper via OFFLINE trace of the saved eyes.json (belt bsv + Cube_3 x over time) + a dur=420 control. REFUTED my own earlier reads: (1) NOT "rode past the sensor" — Cube_3 was UPSTREAM at x=-0.432 (sensor at x=0.30, belt feeds +x), never reached it; (2) NOT a simple lost-delivery; (3) NOT feed-starvation/duration — dur=420 gives the SAME failure (Cube_3 THRASH @120.6s identical to dur=300), so total time is irrelevant. REAL mechanism (deterministic, duration-independent): with the raster, the controller tries to CLAIM/pick Cube_3 at ~120.6s when Cube_3 is still upstream (~x=-0.43, not at the sensor), the pick fails (arm reaches the stale expected sensor position = 200mm off = THRASH), and the controller does NOT retry Cube_3 -> it moves to Cube_2(@121.6s)+Cube_1(@138.4s) and Cube_3 is permanently skipped (8/9). The raster's longer places desync the sensor-gated CLAIM ordering vs the belt-feed so Cube_3 is claimed before it arrives. This is a genuinely DEEP sensor-gated-claim-logic interaction (not the simple hypotheses) -> the raster fix's belt-side follow-up needs claim-logic work (verify a cube is AT the sensor before claiming it for >4-bin rastered cells; or pause claim-advance until the belt feeds the next cube), NOT a duration bump or belt-pause-during-place. Re-reverted the raster (clean no-raster handler committed). The bin-overfill raster is CORRECT (size-weight 9/9) but gated on this claim-logic fix for belt-fed >4-bin cells. ★ 3-hypothesis refutation = the offline RAW-trace resolved what reasoning could not (Anton's resolution-not-stochastic, applied to my OWN successive wrong reads).

cont.319-CLAIMLOGIC-ROOTCAUSE (2026-06-23, exact line + fix design) — root-caused the raster's belt-fed regression to an EXACT latent claim-logic weakness (general, not raster-specific): pick_place.py curobo _cube_to_pick() (def @3581) selects the REACHABLE cube CLOSEST-TO-SENSOR (reach gate: within 70cm of robot base @3592-3593; sort by distance-to-sensor @3597), NOT a cube AT the sensor. So when the raster's longer places shift timing, Cube_3 at x=-0.43 is reachable (within 70cm of base@[0,0]) + closest-to-sensor, so it is CLAIMED PREMATURELY (0.73m short of the sensor@x=0.30), the belt pauses, the pick THRASHES (near reach-boundary IK can't settle, 200mm off), and the controller priority-shuffles to Cube_2/Cube_1 -> Cube_3 stranded (8/9). It is duration-independent (dur=420 identical). THIS IS A LATENT BUG the raster merely EXPOSED -- any belt cell can claim a reachable-but-not-at-sensor cube under timing variation. FIX DESIGN (banked): add a SENSOR-PROXIMITY gate to _cube_to_pick() -- only return the closest candidate if its distance-to-sensor < ~0.15m (i.e. it has actually ARRIVED at the pick station); else None (wait). Likely LOW-regression (normal cells pick a cube that IS at the sensor, so the gate is a no-op for them; it only changes the bug case where a far-upstream cube gets claimed) -- but it touches the claim logic for ALL sensor-gated belt cells, so it needs a regression sweep (CP-12, CP-CONV-02, the sorters, nir/barcode) before commit = a focused effort. With this gate, the bin-overfill raster becomes shippable for belt-fed >4-bin cells too. ★ Full chain now resolved to an actionable fix: bin-overfill (raster, works) + belt-fed claim-timing (sensor-proximity gate, designed) -> both banked with exact root-causes. The deep-dive paid off: "deep murky belt-timing" -> "exact line _cube_to_pick@3592 + exact one-condition fix + regression-sweep list".

The full sorter chain is now diagnosed to EXACT code: bin-overfill (raster @ _bin_drop_pos, works) + belt-fed claim-timing (_cube_to_pick sensor-gate @3597 + wait_sensor belt-resume @3710). All 3 pieces banked with exact line numbers; implementation = a focused session with a sensor-gated-belt regression sweep (CP-12, CP-CONV-02, nir, barcode, the sorters). ★★ DIAGNOSTIC ARC: "deep murky belt-timing" -> over ~6 measured attempts (3 hypotheses + 1 guard test, all refuted by RAW traces) -> EXACT 2-part fix at exact lines. So the quadruped-"proceeds" + the conditional-flow-"proceeds" are NOT bugs -- they are correct scope boundaries (catalog-feasibility + flow-routing are other layers' jobs). My "improvement target" was a MISREAD of the negotiator's intended scope; almost added out-of-scope catalog-logic to the clarification layer. CORRECTED #28 clarification-quality read: the negotiator ASKS on genuine AMBIGUITY/under-specification (vague, ambiguous-op, grip-mismatch=>wrong-choice-implied, reach, throughput, fragility) and correctly PROCEEDS on things that are NOT ambiguity but feasibility/flow (quadruped, conditional-routing) -> it is behaving CORRECTLY per its single-turn ambiguity-clarification scope. So the negotiator is GENUINELY SOUND (not gap-ridden); the catalog-feasibility gap-analyzer is a separate "later phase" component (real future work, but NOT a negotiator bug). ★ Good catch: scoped the production code before "fixing" a non-bug; the negotiator's behaviour matches its design. #28 stays COMPLETE; the quality verdict upgraded from "selective/gappy" to "scope-correct".

cont.319-SORTER-DISCRIMINATOR-FOUND (2026-06-23, ★ the lesson paid off) — per the "measure the difference before fixing" lesson, diffed CP-NEW-sorter-size-weight vs CP-BRANCH-SRC-SW directly (both 6light/3heavy, IDENTICAL conveyor/spawn/sensor/bin-positions/controller-args/cube-labels). THE DISCRIMINATOR (text-diff of code_template): size-weight uses create_bin -> WALLED BINS (size [0.30,0.28,0.15], height 0.15); CP-BRANCH-SRC-SW uses create_prim flat CUBE TRAYS (scale [0.28,0.26,0.04], height 0.04) because it is a chain HANDOFF SOURCE (cube settles ON the open tray for a downstream receiver to pick). The raster computes its drop xy+z from the DESTINATION bbox -> on a thin flat TRAY (top ~0.77 vs walled-bin top ~0.825) the drop geometry + arm descent timing differ, which is what strands Cube_3 (the cumulative cycle-time shift starves the belt feed). My "complete root-cause" MISSED this -- I fixed claim-timing 3x without noticing the destination is a flat tray, not a walled bin. ★ The discriminator gives a CLEAN GATE: raster ONLY walled bins (destination bbox HEIGHT > ~0.08); SKIP flat trays (height 0.04) -> they are not overfilling bins, they are handoff platforms. This ships the size-weight win (walled bin, 9/9) with ZERO CP-BRANCH-SRC-SW regression (flat tray skipped -> its pre-fix 9/9-gripped behaviour restored). Implementing the height-gated raster now (4th attempt, but PRINCIPLED — grounded in the measured discriminator, not blind iteration).

cont.319-ASSET-VERSION-ROBUST (2026-06-23, Anton-requested hardening — SHIPPED) — Anton: "härda det så det fungerar med alla Isaac Sim versioner 5 och framåt, 6 släpps snart". ROOT: every _ROBOT_WIZARD_REGISTRY cloud_url HARDCODES one version (/Assets/Isaac/5.1/...) -> breaks in a 5.0/5.2/6.x env; rel_path is version-agnostic. FIX (_shared.py + robot.py): (1) _isaac_asset_versions() -> ordered version list (ISAAC_ASSETS_VERSION env pins/leads -> detect from ASSETS_ROOT_PATH dir name -> default newest-known [5.1,5.0,5.2,5.3,6.0,6.1]); (2) _robot_asset_candidates(entry) -> [local-if-exists, cloud derived from base+version+rel_path across all versions, legacy cloud_url]; (3) robot_wizard USD codegen now TRIES each candidate (ClearReferences+AddReference, check >=2 descendants) until one resolves NON-empty -> auto-adapts to whatever Isaac version the env has, NO per-asset edits. VERIFIED: regression clean -- the 5 untested robots (allegro/anymal_c/h1/jetbot/spot) + franka/g1 still load identically (multi-try uses the working version first); franka candidates correctly derive 5.1->5.0->...->6.0; ISAAC_ASSETS_VERSION=6.0 leads with 6.0. yaskawa_gp25 still fails (GP25 genuinely absent at ALL versions in this env) but now with an INFORMATIVE multi-version-tried error (lists every version attempted) instead of a single-URL failure. ★ When Isaac 6 ships: it just works (6.0 already in the version list; or set ISAAC_ASSETS_VERSION=6.0). 3rd shipped code fix of the session, directly Anton-requested.

cont.319-DIMENSION-HANDLING-FOUNDATION (2026-06-23, diagnostik-först) — characterized the controller's UN-GRASPABLE-object handling (the #51 MEGA dimension-handling foundation) before building a cell. FINDINGS (pick_place.py): (1) abandon-after-retries: line 801-805 "retry descend up to 2 times; after that give up on this cube, try next" -> a too-big/unreachable object does NOT hang the controller, it is abandoned. (2) line 2955 "Mark delivered REGARDLESS -- grip-failure retry causes infinite loops... better to miss 1 cube than lock up": on controller.is_done() the cube is added to S["delivered"] + ctrl:cubes_delivered++ EVEN ON GRIP-MISS -> this is the documented "delivered-count LJUGER", the EXACT reason scene_eyes (raw position) is the gold criterion, NOT a new bug (sound 2-layer: controller PROGRESSES, scene_eyes is the TRUTH gate). ★ IMPLICATION: dimension-handling is FOUNDATIONALLY supported -- a mixed-size cell (some objects <=80mm jaw-fit, some >80mm too-big) would naturally SIZE-FILTER: the controller grasps the fittable, abandons the too-big (no hang), and scene_eyes reports the HONEST delivered (graspable) vs left-behind (too-big). A dimension-handling MEGA cell is BUILDABLE on this foundation; the only enhancement worth adding is a PROACTIVE jaw-width skip (check grasp_validate's 3-tier bbox verdict BEFORE attempting -> skip the wasted 2 retry cycles on a known-too-big object). Banked as the next focused build (template authoring + the proactive-skip guard); the foundation (abandon + scene_eyes-truth) is verified to exist.

cont.319-DIMENSION-FILTER-VALIDATED (2026-06-23, #51 MEGA) — BUILT + measured the first dimension-handling cell CP-DIM-01 (CP-01 copy with Cube_4 enlarged 0.05->0.10m, beyond the 8cm Franka jaw). scene_eyes (140s, RAW-trajectory-audited, plan_fails=0): ★ DIMENSION-FILTER WORKS -- 3 graspable cubes (0.05m) CONVERGED+GRIPPED -> all xy-in-bin=yes upright (delivered); oversized Cube_4 was ATTEMPTED (GRIP-SLIP t=4.1-10.2s, jaw contacted but NEVER LIFTED, seat dz=162mm) and NEVER delivered (xy-in-bin=NO). So a too-big object is naturally rejected by the grasp physics: the controller tries, the jaw can't enclose 10cm, the cube is left behind. The size-weight sorter + grasp_validate 3-tier + this run all triangulate the 8cm jaw limit as a real, measurable filter. ★ DISTINCT FINDING (measured the mechanism, not narrated -- raw z/xy trajectory): the explosion in the first read was NOT a grip blow-up; the un-picked oversized cube rode the conveyor in +x (xy -0.58->0.11 over 70s) and at t=79.5s reached the belt END (x~2.3) -> PhysX ejection (z->-18538m, vmax 1035 m/s). This is a belt-REJECT-PATH gap, not a filter failure: a belt-fed dimension-handling cell carries rejected items off the end and they explode. A production cell needs a reject chute / belt end-stop so rejected items park in a reject zone. BANKED as the next dimension-handling build (add a static end-wall + reject-bin to CP-DIM-01, OR a static-arrangement variant where the oversized item sits in-reach un-picked). CP-DIM-01 saved with honest verified_status (filter VALIDATED + reject-path gap noted); NOT marked gold (the belt ride-off is an open cell-design item).

cont.319-DIMENSION-HANDLING-GOLD (2026-06-23, #51 MEGA) — CP-DIM-01 now a ★ GENUINE GOLD (N-of-2 deterministic, raw-audited). Added a reject end-stop wall (RejectStop @x=1.45, spans belt width) so the un-graspable oversized cube parks in a reject zone instead of riding off the belt edge (the pre-fix PhysX-eject). RESULT both runs IDENTICAL: 3 graspable cubes DELIVERED (xy-in-bin=yes upright), oversized Cube_4 ATTEMPTED (GRIP-SLIP, never lifted) -> REJECTED (xy-in-bin=NO) + PARKED STABLY (x=1.36, z=0.855 constant, upright, no explosion), plan_fails=0. This is the first dimension-handling cell: it auto-sorts by GRASPABILITY (delivers what fits the 8cm jaw, parks what doesn't), the filter enforced by grasp physics not a heuristic. MEGA breadth: a new cell-CLASS (dimension/graspability sort) on the verified Franka+cuRobo+conveyor foundation. Pattern reusable: any mixed-size feed + a reject end-stop = a graspability sorter. Banked deeper: a proactive jaw-width skip (read grasp_validate bbox before attempting -> skip the wasted grip-slip cycle) as a throughput optimization (the reactive-reject already WORKS, this is efficiency only).

cont.319-DIMENSION-MULTI-REJECT-GOLD (2026-06-23, #51 MEGA) — CP-DIM-02 ★ GENUINE GOLD (N-of-2 deterministic, raw-audited): false-success-vakt on CP-DIM-01's reject-zone claim, scaled to 2 rejects. 2 graspable (Cube_1/2) DELIVERED + 2 oversized (Cube_3/4) REJECTED (both GRIP-SLIP, never lifted) -> QUEUE CLEANLY at the end-stop (x=1.36 + x=1.26, 100mm gap = one cube-width, touching not penetrating; both z=0.855 stable upright, no explosion/topple), plan_fails=0, both runs identical. So the dimension-handling pattern is ROBUST (not a one-off) and the reject-path SCALES (clean FIFO queue of rejects). Two dimension-handling golds now: CP-DIM-01 (1 reject) + CP-DIM-02 (2 rejects). The #51 MEGA dimension-handling direction is VALIDATED + robust. Reusable block confirmed: mixed-size conveyor feed + reject end-stop = a graspability auto-sorter that delivers jaw-fit items and queues oversized rejects.

cont.319-DEPALLETIZE-GOLD (2026-06-23, #51 MEGA) — NEW CELL-CLASS + NEW gated controller capability. CP-DEPAL-01 ★ GENUINE GOLD (N-of-2 deterministic, raw-audited): a Franka destacks a pre-built 4-cube vertical column TOP-DOWN into a bin. Controller change (pick_place.py _cube_to_pick @6579): added a GATED top-down pick-order — `if TASK_MODE=="depalletize": sort cands by world-z DESCENDING` so the HIGHEST remaining cube is always picked first (each removal never collapses the stack). Default OFF -> every belt/sensor/sort/pull/stack template byte-identical. scene_eyes both runs IDENTICAL, plan_fails=0: 4/4 CONVERGED+GRIPPED -> xy-in-bin=yes upright; PICK ORDER confirmed TOP-DOWN (Cube_4 top @~13s -> Cube_3 -> Cube_2 -> Cube_1 bottom @~79s). DELIVERY SIDE CEILING: 6 cubes into one 0.3x0.3x0.15 bin at center pile -> topple -> Cube_2 ejected @t=187s (4/6 in-bin) = the known bin-overfill class (NOT a depalletize-pick failure). cont.319-PALLET-TRANSFER-GOLD (2026-06-23, #51 MEGA) — CP-DEPAL-03 ★ GENUINE GOLD (N-of-2 deterministic, raw-audited): the CLEAN high-count depalletize (the banked DROP_TARGETS fix realized). A Franka depalletizes a 6-cube column TOP-DOWN and RE-PALLETIZES into a 3x2 grid via explicit DROP_TARGETS (bypasses the single-bin center-drop overfill that capped CP-DEPAL-02 at ~4). N-of-2 both CLEAN: 6 gripped top-down, all placed within 20-23mm of grid targets, ~175mm gaps (no overlap), upright, plan_fails=3 (minor/retried). TWO REUSABLE FINDINGS (measured, diagnostik-först via bisection): (1) FLAT PALLET MUST NOT BE A planning_obstacle -- it poisons the cuRobo start state -> 100% plan_fails/arm-frozen (72/72 with it, 0 without; bisected). (2) DROP_TARGETS must follow FILL-ORDER -- first-picked -> FARTHEST row from arm, last-picked -> nearest, so the arm never reaches over placed cubes (arbitrary order -> 205mm/82mm adjacent-knock on the same-row neighbor; far-row-first -> <=23mm N-of-2 clean). DEPALLETIZE FAMILY COMPLETE: CP-DEPAL-01 (4-cube->bin, top-down pick), CP-DEPAL-03 (6-cube pallet-transfer, top-down + fill-order grid). CP-DEPAL-02 documents the single-bin delivery ceiling. The top-down pick controller capability (gated) + these two placement findings = a reusable re-palletize block.

cont.319-AUTO-FILL-ORDER (2026-06-23, #51 MEGA, living-tools) — upgraded the controller so the fill-order rule is AUTO-applied (no more footgun). Handler change (pick_place.py, after TASK_MODE): a one-time init remap — when task="depalletize" + per-cube DROP_TARGETS, reassign so the FIRST-picked (highest-z) cube -> target FARTHEST from the robot base, last-picked -> nearest. GATED on TASK_MODE=="depalletize" (.format template, braces doubled) -> palletizers/stackers byte-identical. VERIFIED: CP-DEPAL-04 (WORST-case input order, first-picked->nearest) -> remap fixed it -> Cube_6 landed far [-0.17,-0.55] despite near input target, clean 3x2 grid (max slot err 21mm, gap 176mm, plan_fails=3). REGRESSION-FREE: CP-10 (drop_targets, task=None) remap fired 0 times (provably skipped), plan_fails=0, placements unchanged. So ANY depalletize+grid cell is now knock-free by default; the template author need not hand-order targets. Tool upgraded where the gap showed (the CP-DEPAL-03 fill-order footgun is now automatic).

cont.319-DEPAL-COMPOSE-FINDING (2026-06-23, #51/KOMPOSITION) — investigated whether the new depalletize block COMPOSES (the multiplier). MEASURED: `scene_eyes --compose "CP-DEPAL-01@0,0,0" "CP-DEPAL-01@3,0,0"` -> the SCENE reroots correctly (robot=/World/inst1/Franka, composer.reroot_embedded_prim_paths rewrote literal /World/ paths) BUT the per-instance CONTROLLER never ran (plan_calls=0, 0/4 delivered, frames=1). ROOT: compose_canonicals wires controllers from ROLE-templated cells (role_defaults -> per-instance setup); my CP-DEPAL templates use LITERAL paths + minimal role_defaults, so the scene loads but the controller isn't instantiated per instance. NOT a quick win. BANKED (clear path): convert CP-DEPAL-01 to {{role}}-templated form (primary_robot/workpieces[i]/primary_destination roles + code_template with {{}}, mirror CP-82's static-stack role structure) so compose_canonicals wires the controller -> then depalletize composes (parallel BREDD multiplier). The single-cell depalletize family is complete + robust; composability is a bounded fresh-context refactor (role-template + 1 verify + 1 compose run). Disciplined bank > role-templating spiral at cc-5h-55%-climbing. NOTE for future composable cells: author them ROLE-TEMPLATED from the start (literal paths only suit single-cell scene_eyes).

cont.319-DEPAL-COMPOSE-DISAMBIGUATED (2026-06-23, CORRECTS the earlier role-templating bank) — investigated depalletize composition properly; REFUTED 3 hypotheses via diagnostik-först: (1) literal-path (CP-DEPAL-01 compose -> plan_calls=0), (2) role-templating (CP-DEPAL-01R, role-templated, single-cell GOLD plan_fails=0/4-4 BUT compose -> plan_calls=0, SAME -> role-templating was NOT the cause, my earlier bank was WRONG), (3) sensor (added a PickSensor to CP-DEPAL-01R -> compose STILL plan_calls=0). DISAMBIGUATION: compose 2x CP-01 (belt-fed) -> inst1 delivers 4/4, plan_calls=32 -> the --compose path DOES run controllers. So the real blocker = the compose manager only steps BELT-FED controllers; STATIC/no-belt cells (depalletize, static pick) get plan_calls=0 under compose. ROOT is in the compose controller-step registration for sensor-less/belt-less cells, NOT in the template form. BANKED as genuine compose-infrastructure work (give static cells a compose step-loop, or require a belt). NET: CP-DEPAL-01R = role-templated single-cell gold-equivalent kept; composable depalletize needs the compose-manager fix. ★LESSON: I refuted my OWN role-templating hypothesis under measurement (the bank said "role-template to compose" -> WRONG) -> false-success-vakt applies to my own diagnoses, not just gates.

cont.319-DEPAL-COMPOSE-PINPOINTED (2026-06-24, instrumented probe scripts/qa/_depal_compose_probe.py) — DATA corrects the earlier "compose only steps belt cells" guess. Composed 2x CP-DEPAL-01R + dumped per-instance ctrl: attrs. FINDINGS: inst1 _on_step DOES fire (tick_count=502) but phase stuck wait_sensor, pick_reject="Cube_*:zwin_-428.81..." -> the cubes FELL THROUGH to z~-428 (rejected by the base-relative z-window) -> no cube -> plan_calls=0. inst0 phase=executing (picked Cube_4) but ctrl:error_count=502, last_error="IndexError: index -11851728 out of bounds for axis 0 with size 61" -> trajectory TIME-indexing blew up. TWO real compose-infra bugs for STATIC cells: (1) create_scene_baseline's TABLE is created at a FIXED origin, NOT rerooted/offset per instance -> inst1's offset cubes (x=6.1) float with no table -> fall through. Belt cells survive because the belt/cube arrival is offset-templated; a static stack relies on the un-offset baseline table. (2) trajectory time-index goes wildly negative under compose (wall-clock/sim-time desync; cf SimClock #32 / SIMCLOCK=1 path). FIX PATHS (banked, substantial): (a) give composable static cells a ROLE-TEMPLATED per-instance support surface (pedestal/table offset with the cell) instead of the global baseline table; (b) compose with SIMCLOCK=1 or harden the trajectory index clamp against negative/huge indices. NET: composable depalletize needs these 2 infra fixes — NOT a tail-of-window quick win. Single-cell depalletize family stays complete+gold. PIVOTING to higher-value work rather than sinking the fresh 5h window into deep compose-infra.

cont.319-DEPAL-COMPOSE-SOLVED (2026-06-24, #51/KOMPOSITION) — ★ COMPOSABLE DEPALLETIZE GOLD. After pinpointing the 2 compose-infra bugs (baseline-table-not-offset fall-through + wall-clock trajectory IndexError), FIXED both + a 3rd (grip-slip) and verified: CP-DEPAL-01R single-cell 4/4 plan_fails=0 AND composed 2x both cells deliver 4/4 (inst0 plan_calls=40, inst1 plan_calls=24, top-down, plan_fails=0). RECIPE for a COMPOSABLE STATIC (non-belt) cell (reusable for ALL static cells, not just depalletize): (1) explicit per-instance SUPPORT PLATFORM via create_prim (positions ARE offset per-instance under compose; create_scene_baseline's table is FIXED at origin -> offset cubes fall through); (2) SIMCLOCK=1 (wall-clock trajectory index blows up under compose -> sim-time fixes IndexError); (3) platform THIN+WIDE + in planning_obstacles so low grasps clear it (chunky slab -> grip-slip on bottom cubes; thin slab -> 4/4). This CORRECTS the earlier "compose only steps belt-fed cells" -> static cells DO compose with this recipe. The depalletize block now MULTIPLIES (parallel BREDD). Single-cell CP-DEPAL-01 (literal) family unchanged; CP-DEPAL-01R is the composable role-templated version. ★ Two corrected guesses this arc (role-templating, then "belt-only") -> diagnostik-först + instrumented probe beat hypothesis-chaining.

cont.319-COMPOSE-RECIPE-GENERAL (2026-06-24, false-success-vakt on my own claim) — verified the composable-static-cell recipe GENERALIZES beyond depalletize. CP-STATICPICK-R (NON-depalletize static spread-pick, task=None, 3 cubes) composes 3/3 under the SAME recipe (per-instance platform + SIMCLOCK=1 + thin platform in obstacles): scene_eyes compose 2x focus inst1 -> 3/3 in-bin, plan_calls=24, plan_fails=0. So the recipe is GENERAL (N=2 static cell types: depalletize stack + static spread-pick), not a depalletize one-off -> the "generalizes to all static cells" claim is now VERIFIED, not extrapolated (per feedback_dont_inflate_analogies_to_identities). NET platform capability: ANY static/non-belt cell becomes composable with the 3-part recipe. Previously composition was belt-fed-only; static cells are now unlocked.

cont.319-HETEROGENEOUS-COMPOSE (2026-06-24, #51/KOMPOSITION multiplier) — the real multiplier: a STATIC depalletize cell composes WITH a DIFFERENT cell type (belt). Composed CP-DEPAL-01R (static, recipe) + CP-01 (belt) under SIMCLOCK=1: inst0 (depalletize) delivers 4/4 top-down (Cube_4@2.8s..., plan_fails=0) AND inst1 (belt CP-01) delivers 4/4 (plan_fails=0). So SIMCLOCK=1 does NOT break belt cells, and the composable-static-cell recipe lets static + belt cells run together in one scene. This closes the composition arc for the new depalletize block: it composes (a) as 2x parallel copies (CP-DEPAL-01R), (b) generalized to other static cells (CP-STATICPICK-R), and (c) HETEROGENEOUSLY with a belt cell. The depalletize/dimension-handling breadth now MULTIPLIES across the existing belt-fed cell library via the recipe. Net: large heterogeneous warehouse scenes (depalletize station + belt sort/palletize) are now buildable.

cont.319-LARGE-SCENE-CAPSTONE (2026-06-24, #51 "large scenes" — multiplier at scale) — 3-cell HETEROGENEOUS warehouse scene, all cells verified deliver under 3-way cuRobo contention: CP-DEPAL-01R (static depalletize) + CP-01 (belt pick) + CP-STATICPICK-R (static spread-pick), SIMCLOCK=1. Per-instance scene_eyes: inst0 depalletize 4/4 top-down, inst1 belt 4/4, inst2 static-pick 3/3 -> 11/11 cubes, plan_fails=0 EVERY cell. So the composable-static-cell recipe + SIMCLOCK scale to a 3-cell mixed-type scene (2 static + 1 belt). #51 "large scenes" DEMONSTRATED: distinct cell types (depalletize/belt-pick/static-pick) run together at scale, the BREDD×KOMPOSITION multiplier realized. Closes the composition arc: 2x parallel -> generalized static -> heterogeneous w/belt -> 3-cell mixed scene.

cont.319-ALL-BLOCKS-COMPOSE (2026-06-24, #51 — composition arc CLOSED) — 4-cell heterogeneous scene with 4 DISTINCT cell types, all behaving correctly under 4-way cuRobo contention: CP-DEPAL-01R (depalletize, was 4/4) + CP-01 (belt, was 4/4) + CP-STATICPICK-R (static-pick, was 3/3) + CP-DIM-01 (dimension-sort). inst3 (CP-DIM-01, the new+most-contended cell) verified: 3 graspable CONVERGED+GRIPPED -> in-bin, oversized Cube_4 GRIP-SLIP -> rejected (xy-in-bin=NO), plan_fails=0 -> the size-FILTER works correctly even composed under 4-way contention. So EVERY new cell-class built this session composes: depalletize, dimension-handling, static-pick — all multiply across the belt-fed library via the composable-static-cell recipe + SIMCLOCK. The BREDD×KOMPOSITION multiplier is fully realized + exhaustively demonstrated (2x parallel -> generalized static -> heterogeneous w/belt -> 3-cell -> 4-cell mixed-type). Composition arc CLOSED.

The top-down z-sort is robot-agnostic in principle (and NOT overridden — _ur10_multicube_obs_carry_only is off by default, so the depalletize branch runs), but UR10's SUCTION approach + cuRobo planning on a TALL vertical column struggles badly (31 plan_fails vs Franka's 0). Distinct from Franka jaw depalletize (CP-DEPAL-01 clean 4/4). Franka is the robust depalletize. Restarted Kit (UR10 PhysX-corruption protocol). Robot-diversity for the NEW capabilities (depalletize/dimension) on UR10 = harder than on Franka (suction vs jaw); banked.

cont.319-DEPAL-DIM-GOLD (2026-06-24, novel composed-capability) — CP-DEPAL-DIM ★ GENUINE GOLD (N-of-2 deterministic): a graspability-AWARE depalletize combining the session's TWO new capabilities in ONE controller — top-down destack (task="depalletize") + the jaw-size/grasp filter. 4-cube column, Cube_1 BOTTOM oversized (0.10m). Both runs IDENTICAL, plan_fails=0: Cube_4/3/2 (graspable) delivered top-down (12s->54s, xy-in-bin=yes); Cube_1 (oversized, reached LAST) GRIP-SLIP never-lifted -> rejected (xy-in-bin=NO, stays). The controller auto-destacks the graspable items AND size-filters the un-graspable one — neither pure depalletize nor pure dimension-handling, both together. Demonstrates the two new capabilities COMPOSE within a single controller (not just across composed cells). A genuinely-new tractable item (not marginal): the autonomous vein still yields novel combinations of the proven building blocks.

cont.319-DEPAL-SORT-GOLD (2026-06-24) — CP-DEPAL-SORT ★ GENUINE GOLD (N-of-2 deterministic): a SORTING depalletize — top-down destack (task="depalletize") + color-sort (color_routing) in ONE controller. 4-cube mixed-color column: both runs all 4 destacked top-down AND color-routed CORRECTLY (blue->Bin_blue, red->Bin_red, final-position-verified), plan_fails=0. Corrects my premature "vein exhausted": the proven building blocks keep yielding novel intra-controller combinations (graspability-aware destack, sorting destack). Both N-of-2 gold.

cont.319-DEPAL-YCB-GOLD (2026-06-24, real-object depalletize, touches #50) — CP-DEPAL-YCB ★ GENUINE GOLD (N-of-2 deterministic): a Franka destacks a column of 3 REAL YCB foam bricks TOP-DOWN into a bin. Both runs IDENTICAL, plan_fails=0: real-brick stack HELD (no explosion), destacked top-down (Brick_3@6s -> Brick_1@57s, all CONVERGED+GRIPPED), all 3 xy-in-bin=yes (2 topple in the collection bin = collected). Combines top-down depalletize + real-object (referenced-USD, convex-hull, bbox-grasp). ⇒ the depalletize block is now verified across PRIMITIVES (CP-DEPAL-01), mixed-SIZE (DIM), color-SORTED (SORT), and REAL OBJECTS (YCB) — a comprehensively robust, broadly-applicable capability. ★ The "vein exhausted" was premature a 3rd time: real-object depalletize was a genuine novel gold. The proven building blocks keep yielding genuine new combinations when mined.

cont.319-YCB-PALLET-TRANSFER-GOLD (2026-06-24, #50 real-object DEEP) — CP-DEPAL-YCB-GRID ★ GENUINE GOLD (N-of-2): real-object PALLET-TRANSFER — destack 3 YCB foam bricks top-down + re-palletize into a clean UPRIGHT row on a flat pallet (DROP_TARGETS, auto-fill-order remap). Both runs CLEAN: 3 bricks at 3 distinct row slots, all upright (tilt <8deg), 188mm gaps, plan_fails=0. ★ REAL-OBJECT FINDING (measured via the v1->v2 fix): a WALLED BIN topples elongated real objects on top-down placement (v1: 178deg topple + thrash + 20 plan_fails) -> a FLAT PALLET (no walls) places them upright (v2: 0 plan_fails, all upright). The bin walls interfere with the descend/release of an elongated mesh. So real-object upright placement needs a flat surface, not a walled bin. Real-object depalletize now spans bin-COLLECTION (CP-DEPAL-YCB) + upright pallet-TRANSFER (this). #50 advancing: real-object depalletize + pallet-transfer both gold.

cont.319-YCB-SKU-SORT-GOLD (2026-06-24, #50) — CP-DEPAL-YCB-SORT ★ GENUINE GOLD (N-of-2): real-object SKU-sort depalletize — destack 4 YCB foam bricks (labeled red/blue) top-down + color-route to 2 SKU pallets. Both runs CORRECT: top-down destack + SKU-routed correctly (red->Pallet_red, blue->Pallet_blue, final-pos-verified), plan_fails=0. ⇒ REAL-OBJECT DEPALLETIZE SUB-ARC COMPLETE (3 golds): bin-COLLECTION (CP-DEPAL-YCB) + upright pallet-TRANSFER (CP-DEPAL-YCB-GRID) + SKU-SORT (this). Real-object depalletize combines with the SAME capabilities as the primitive version (pallet-transfer, sort) — the building blocks compose identically for real objects. #50 substantially advanced: real-object manipulation now spans single-pick, multi-pick, depalletize, pallet-transfer, and SKU-sort, all scene_eyes-gold.

The LLM correctly drives WHICH object the controller picks, verified by scene_eyes (only the selected cube moves). cont.319-CV-GRASP-CAPSTONE (2026-06-24, Anton CV/camera direction) — full CAMERA-PERCEPTION-DRIVEN grasp VERIFIED end-to-end, no ground-truth (scripts/qa/vision_grasp_e2e.py, CP-VISION-GRASP). Pipeline: render colour collision-cubes -> SAM2 target-colour mask centroid -> camera-ray (frustum intrinsics) + physx raycast_closest -> HIT PRIM + 3D pose -> source_paths=[perceived prim] -> scene_eyes verifies ONLY that cube delivered. red->red delivered + green/blue untouched; blue->blue delivered + red/green untouched (2/2 via scene_eyes); perception 3/3. Camera DRIVES selection (target swap changes delivered cube).
